items.body: Barkley (hamstring/back) is participating in Thursday's practice, Brooks Kubena of The Athletic reports. After sitting out Wednesday's practice due to existing hamstring and back injuries, Barkley is returning to drills one day later, which is one day earlier than a week ago. He thus appears to be a bit healthier this time around, but his activity level will become known once the Eagles post their second Week 9 practice report Thursday.

items.head: Not spotted at practice
items.body: Barkley wasn't present for the media-access portion of Wednesday's practice, Brooks Kubena of The Athletic reports. Barkley may still be tending to the hamstring and back issues that he impacted his practice reps last week, but Wednesday's injury report will reveal if he indeed was a non-participant and also the reason for his absence. Jaydon Blue is the only healthy RB on the Eagles' active roster, though practice-squad member Elijah Mitchell tallied 11 carries for 34 yards and four catches (on six targets) for three yards while splitting the backfield with Barkley this past Sunday at Washington.

items.head: Receives assurances he won't be dealt
items.body: Barkley said after Sunday's 27-10 loss to the Commanders that he has received assurances from the Eagles front office that he will remain with the team beyond the Nov. 10 trade deadline, Tim McManus of ESPN.com reports. "The whole time my mindset was, we have a little issue going on right now and I feel like I'm the type of player and the type of leader that can help us get out of it," Barkley said. "And I want to be one of the reasons why we fix it." After dropping their sixth straight game Sunday, the Eagles now sit at 2-6 on the season and could be motivated to explore moving veteran players for draft capital ahead of the deadline. Barkley -- who is under contract through 2028 -- apparently won't be among the pieces the Eagles consider moving, as the team is counting on re-emerging as a playoff contender next season rather than embracing a long-term rebuilding effort. Though he'll be suiting up for a Week 9 matchup with the division-leading Giants, Barkley could continue to have his playing time managed while he gets ramped back up from hamstring and back injuries. He played just 22 of the Eagles' 68 offensive snaps in the loss to Wash

items.head: Sharing backfield with Hall
items.body: Jets coach Aaron Glenn declined to elaborate on the distribution of carries between Allen and Breece Hall, who will return from a five-game absence for Sunday's matchup with Kansas City, ESPN's Rich Cimini reports. Allen averaged 18.6 carries for 100.8 yards and 0.4 TDs over the past four games, adding 2.6 catches for 14.0 yards on 3.4 targets while playing at least 78 percent of snaps each week. He won't get that kind of workload with Hall back in the lineup, but it is possible that this turns into a hot-hand situation where Allen still has a chance to take the majority of carries if he outplays his backfield mate. Both Glenn and Hall said earlier this week that Hall is still viewed as the starter.

items.head: Career-high 147 rushing yards in Week 8
items.body: Allen rushed 21 times for 147 yards and a touchdown while catching both of his targets for six yards in Sunday's 38-33 loss to the Raiders. Allen made a fifth consecutive start in the absence of Breece Hall (quadriceps) and exceeded 100 scrimmage yards for the fourth consecutive game. The 2024 fourth-round pick set a new career high with 147 rushing yards, surpassing Allen's 116 yards on the ground in the Week 5 win over the Browns. Allen scored his third rushing touchdown of the season on a 21-yard run in the third quarter to give the Jets a 30-21 lead, but the Raiders closed the game on a 17-3 run to drop the Jets to 2-6. If Hall's ready to return in Week 9 against the Chiefs, the Jets could opt for a backfield split between Allen and Hall.

items.head: Headed for another start Sunday
items.body: Allen is slated to serve as the Jets' starting running back Sunday against the Raiders, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports. For a second week in a row, fellow running back Breece Hall (quadriceps) is listed questionable to play, but he was inactive in Week 7, and he's considered unlikely to play again in Week 8, per Rapoport. Assuming Hall is officially ruled out when the Jets release their inactive list 90 minutes prior to the 1 p.m. ET kickoff, Allen should be headed for another heavy workload out of the New York backfield. In the Jets' last four games sans Hall, Allen combined for 83 touches for 421 yards from scrimmage and one rushing touchdown.

items.head: No designation for Week 9
items.body: Watson (ribs) doesn't have a designation for Sunday's contest at New England. Despite being limited on all three of the Packers' Week 9 injury reports due to the broken rib he sustained during last Thursday's win against the Panthers, Watson will be available to Green Bay's offense. It stands to reason he'll wear some sort of protection around his midsection Sunday, but he nonetheless is a plug-and-play option due to his 42-708-6 line on 66 targets through the first eight games of the campaign.

items.body: Watson (ribs) was a limited practice participant Thursday, Rob Demovsky of ESPN.com reports. Watson now has back-to-back capped sessions under his belt to begin Week 9 prep, which stems from the broken rib that he suffered during last Thursday's win against the Panthers. He'll have one more chance Friday to get back to full participation, at which point the Packers may tag him with a designation for Sunday's contest at New England.

items.body: Watson (ribs) is wearing pads for Thursday's practice, Wes Hodkiewicz of the Packers' official site reports. Watson was listed as a limited participant at Wednesday's practice after sustaining a rib injury in Green Bay's Week 8 win over the Panthers. His participation level Thursday has yet to be revealed, but it's a good sign that Watson is able to practice in pads and take contact as the Packers prepare to face the Patriots on Sunday.

items.head: Limited Wednesday
items.body: Watson (ribs) practiced in a limited capacity Wednesday, Matt Schneidman of The Athletic reports. After making a visit to the hospital during last Thursday's win against the Panthers, Watson was able to return and finished with eight catches (on 10 targets) for 113 yards. Afterward, he was revealed to have a broken rib, which likely will be an injury he plays through while managing pain tolerance. In any case, Friday's injury report will unveil whether or not he enters the weekend with a designation for Sunday's game at New England.

items.head: Managing rib soreness ahead of Week 9
items.body: Packers passing game coordinator Jason Vrable said Monday that Watson (ribs) is sore but "doing great," Matt Schneidman of The Athletic reports. Watson suffered a broken rib during this past Thursday's win over the Panthers, and while Vrable notes with regard to Watson's status for this Sunday's game against the Patriots, "We'll see as the week goes," he added that the wideout will do everything possible to get his body ready in advance of Week 9 action. In the event that Watson is unavailable, added reps behind Matthew Golden will be available for Savion Williams, Bo Melton and J. Michael Sturdivant.

items.body: Kamara (rest/back) doesn't have a designation for Sunday's game versus the Browns. Kamara went from DNP due to rest/back Wednesday to limited Thursday and finally full Friday, paving the way for him to be available to the Saints backfield. With fellow RB CJ Donaldson (shoulder/concussion) sidelined this weekend, it'll be Kamara and Kendre Miller to handle the load Sunday.

items.head: Limited Thursday
items.body: Kamara (rest/back) was limited at Thursday's practice, Katherine Terrell of ESPN.com reports. Kamara followed up Wednesday's absence from practice with some activity one day later as he eases into the week due to a lingering back issue. Friday's injury report will reveal if he has a designation for Sunday's game against the Browns.

items.head: Returns to practice Thursday
items.body: Kamara (rest/back) returned to practice Thursday, Nick Underhill of NewOrleans.Football reports. The veteran RB was back on the field Thursday after getting a rest day to open the practice week. Kamara has also dealt with a back issue that limited his practice participation in recent weeks. The Saints are coming off a bye, so the added time off likely bodes well for Kamara being closer to full strength heading into Week 9 against the Browns. New Orleans' practice report will provide insight on Kamara's participation level, but he seems to be trending in the right direction regardless.

items.head: Alvin Kamara (Back) is Questionable
items.body: Kamara (rest/back) returned to practice Thursday, Nick Underhill of NewOrleans.Football reports.

items.head: DNP due to rest, back
items.body: Kamara (rest/back) didn't practice Wednesday. The Saints cited rest and a back injury -- the latter of which impacted his practice reps in each of the three games before the team's Week 8 bye -- as the reasons for Kamara's absence to begin Week 9 prep. During that three-contest stretch, he tallied 27 touches for 137 yards from scrimmage and one receiving TD. Kamara will have two more opportunities to practice this week and put himself in a position to avoid a designation for Sunday's contest against the Browns.

items.head: Another huge opportunity?
items.body: Mitchell and Omar Cooper will be the Jets' top wide receivers with Garrett Wilson (concussion) unavailable for Sunday's game at Kansas City, ESPN's Rich Cimini reports. Mitchell is coming off the best performance of his career -- a 7-141-1 receiving line on 26 routes (nine targets) in last week's 38-33 loss to Las Vegas. Cooper also ran 26 routes but finished without a target, despite topping 100 yards in back-to-back games beforehand. Both wide receivers now have a big opportunity with Wilson out of the lineup against a Kansas City defense that's missing cornerbacks Mansoor Delane (shoulder) and L'Jarius Sneed (IR - knee).

items.head: Career-high 142 yards in Week 8
items.body: Mitchell caught seven of nine targets for 142 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 38-33 loss to the Raiders. Mitchell didn't catch any of his three targets in the Week 7 loss to Miami after returning from a four-game absence due to a finger injury, but he bounced back with a career-best Week 8 performance. His top highlights Sunday were a 12-yard touchdown catch in the second quarter and a 47-yard reception in the fourth quarter. Garrett Wilson led the team with 12 targets while Omar Cooper went without a target after back-to-back games with more than 100 yards and a TD. The 2-6 Jets could try to get all three of their talented young wideouts involved in Week 9, when they will likely be playing catch-up against the Chiefs.

items.head: Cleared for Sunday
items.body: Boston (calf) was a full participant in Friday's practice and doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game at New Orleans, Chris Easterling of the Akron Beacon Journal reports. With Boston upgrading from limited sessions Wednesday and Thursday to full participation Friday, he should be fine for his usual role as a near-every-down player in a young Cleveland offense. It'll be his first chance to work with Shedeur Sanders extensively outside of a practice environment, as the Browns reportedly won't start Deshaun Watson (head) even if he clears concussion protocol before the game.

items.head: Denzel Boston (injury) is Active
items.body: Boston (calf) was a full participant in Friday's practice and doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game at New Orleans, Chris Easterling of the Akron Beacon Journal reports.

items.head: Remains limited Thursday
items.body: Boston (calf) remained limited in Thursday's practice, Mary Kay Cabot of The Cleveland Plain Dealer reports. Boston dealt with a foot issue a couple weeks ago, but the calf injury is new this week. The rookie wideout has been scuffling after a hot start to the season. Perhaps the likely insertion of Shedeur Sanders this Sunday against the Saints can help Boston regain his big-play ability. Boston is a low-floor, upside WR4 for fantasy.

items.body: Boston (calf) remained limited in Thursday's practice, Mary Kay Cabot of The Cleveland Plain Dealer reports.

items.head: Limited by calf injury Wednesday
items.body: Boston was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice due to a calf injury, Scott Petrak of the Elyria Chronicle-Telegram reports. Boston made appearances on the injury report in Weeks 6 and 7 due to a foot issue, but he's tending to a new health concern coming out of this past Sunday's 27-6 loss to the Steelers. The rookie wideout will have two more chances this week to upgrade to full practice, and if he does, he should head into Sunday's game in New Orleans without an injury designation.

items.head: Six snags in loss
items.body: Boston caught six of 11 targets for 37 yards during Sunday's 27-6 loss to the Steelers. Boston entered Week 8 having caught just four of 13 targets for 42 yards over the previous two games, so Sunday's output was a step in the right direction. The wide receiver's 11 targets were a new career high, and he ranked second behind tight end Harold Fannin (12) in the category versus Pittsburgh. Boston has now reeled in 26 of 53 targets for 409 yards and three touchdowns over the first eight games of the 2026 campaign.

items.head: CJ Donaldson (Shoulder) is Questionable

items.head: Set for expanded workload again in Week 9
items.body: With TreVeyon Henderson (illness) ruled out for Week 9, Stevenson is set to handle an expanded workload Sunday against the Packers, Mark Daniels of MassLive.com reports. Henderson will miss a second straight game tending to medical issue. With the second-year running back out last week against Miami, Stevenson logged 76.7 percent of the offensive snaps and handled a season-high 19 carries, turning them into 82 scoreless yards. He also caught three passes on three targets. Stevenson will be a volume-driven, home-favorite RB1/2 for fantasy against Green Bay, while Corey Kiner will step into the RB2 role again.

items.head: Racks up 90 scrimmage yards Sunday
items.body: Stevenson carried the ball 19 times for 82 yards and caught all three of his targets for eight yards in Sunday's 24-19 win over the Dolphins. With TreVeyon Henderson (illness) unavailable, Stevenson led the Patriots in rushing yards and scrimmage yards, although he wasn't able to get into the end zone. His 19 totes and 82 rushing yards were both season highs. The veteran back's workload in Week 9 against the Packers will depend somewhat on Henderson's health, but Stevenson appears to be Mike Vrabel's most trusted option in the backfield, and through eight games he's on pace to top 1,000 scrimmage yards for the first time since 2022.

items.head: Listed questionable for Sunday
items.body: Tyson (hamstring) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Browns, Katherine Terrell of ESPN.com reports. With Tyson having logged limited practices after the Saints opened his 21-day window to return from injured reserve Wednesday, Friday's designation gives the rookie a chance to make his long-awaited regular-season NFL debut. There's been no indication one way or the other on what the Saints' plans are for Tyson this week. Devaughn Vele and Bryce Lance would be the biggest losers in terms of playing time and targets once Tyson does debut.

items.head: Remains limited Thursday
items.body: Tyson (hamstring) remained a limited participant at Thursday's practice, Katherine Terrell of ESPN.com reports. Tyson has logged consecutive limited practices since having his 21-day window to return from IR opened Wednesday. The rookie first-round pick could make his NFL regular-season debut as soon as Sunday against the Browns, though the Saints may want him to log at least one full practice before seeing game action. For his part, Nick Underhill of NewOrleans.Football suggested that from his point of view Tyson didn't look limited Thursday. In any case, the wideout's return to action, be it this week or next, would be proceeded by an official move adding him to the 53-man roster.

items.head: Limited in return Wednesday
items.body: Tyson (hamstring) turned in a limited practice Wednesday, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports. This is a big step in the right direction for Tyson, whose 21-day practice window is now open. The rookie has been sidelined since late in camp with a significant hamstring injury. A limited practice after a long time away from the field does not guarantee he'll be ready to go for Sunday's game against the Browns. However, Tyson's debut is on the horizon, even if it is not this week.

items.head: Returning to practice Wednesday
items.body: Tyson (hamstring) is slated to resume practicing with the Saints on Wednesday, Nick Underhill of NewOrleans.Football reports. The Saints are expected to officially open the wide receiver's 21-day evaluation window as they kick off Week 9 prep ahead of Sunday's game against the Browns. Given that the strained right hamstring has kept him off the field since Aug. 13, Tyson may need more than one week of practices to get himself back into playing shape, but the Saints haven't necessarily ruled the rookie first-round pick out from making his NFL debut against Cleveland. Whenever he's deemed ready to play, Tyson could immediately push Devaughn Vele for the Saints' No. 2 receiver job.

items.head: Uncertain to practice this week
items.body: Saints head coach Kellen Moore said that the Saints will decide by Wednesday whether to open Tyson's (hamstring) 21-day practice window this week, Nick Underhill of NewOrleans.Football reports. Adam Schefter of ESPN reported over the weekend that Tyson could have a chance at making his NFL debut as soon as this coming Sunday against the Browns, but until the Saints formally clear the wideout to practice, a target date for him to play will remain somewhat muddled. The No. 8 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft, Tyson had a checkered medical history during his collegiate career, and the right hamstring strain he sustained in mid-August has only added to the long-term concerns about his durability. However, the 6-foot-2, 203-pound Tyson is undoubtedly talented, and he'll have a fairly clear path to the No. 2 receiver gig if he can get healthy.

items.head: Could debut in Week 9
items.body: Tyson (hamstring) could be reinstated from injured reserve and make his season debut as soon as next Sunday versus the Browns, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports. The Saints haven't cleared Tyson to practice since he strained his right hamstring during an Aug. 13 training camp workout, but the rookie first-round pick sounds like he could have his 21-day evaluation window opened in Week 9. Due to the length of his absence, Tyson may not be ready to play against Cleveland even if he checks out well in practice during the upcoming week, but in any case, he doesn't appear far away from making his NFL debut. Whenever he's activated, Tyson could push Devaughn Vele for the No. 2 receiver role behind top target Chris Olave.

items.head: Six total TDs in wild win
items.body: Burrow completed 38 of 48 passes for 462 yards with five touchdowns and three interceptions and added three carries for 10 yards and another score in the Bengals' 43-36 overtime win over the Titans on Sunday. A Titans offense that had been mostly moribund all season unexpectedly came to life Sunday, requiring Burrow to remain aggressive throughout the afternoon. While that helped lead to his season-high three interceptions, it was also unsurprisingly a boon for his fantasy production, as the 2020 first overall pick finished with his second 400-yard performance of the season and a season-high five TD tosses. Burrow had his rapport with top receivers Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins working throughout the afternoon, as he connected with the duo a combined 21 times for 296 yards and three touchdowns. items.head: 3 ways Browns QB Shedeur Sanders can show growth vs. Saints
items.body: The opportunity is a big one as the second-year quarterback's first start of the season comes at a critical time.

items.head: Will start Sunday
items.body: Sanders will start at quarterback Sunday against the Saints, Scott Petrak of the Elyria Chronicle-Telegram reports. Coach Todd Monken said the move is because Deshaun Watson (concussion) missed so much practice time this week. Watson has been one of the worst statistical quarterbacks in the league over the last month, so Sanders could potentially keep the job if he has a good game against the Saints. His insertion under center doesn't change the outlook of the offense, as both Watson and Sanders are game-manager types.

items.head: Browns to start Sanders at QB vs. Saints with Watson in protocol
items.body: The Browns will start Shedeur Sanders at quarterback against the Saints as Deshaun Watson remains in the concussion protocol.

items.head: Could start Week 9 with Watson in protocol
items.body: Sanders could be needed to start Sunday's game at New Orleans after Deshaun Watson was placed in concussion protocol when he experienced symptoms Monday, Mary Kay Cabot of The Cleveland Plain Dealer reports. During this past Sunday's 27-6 loss to the Steelers, Watson briefly departed the game in the first quarter after a helmet-to-helmet hit from safety Jaquan Brisker. Sanders checked in and completed both of his pass attempts for two yards across four total plays before Watson was cleared to return for the Browns' next possession. However, with the concussion symptoms surfacing a day later, Watson's availability for Week 9 is now in jeopardy. Watson will still have time to clear the five-step protocol ahead of Sunday, but expect Sanders to at least get some reps in with the first-team offense Wednesday during the team's first practice of the week.

items.head: Won't play Sunday against Green Bay
items.body: Henderson (illness) won't play Sunday against the Packers, Evan Lazar of the Patriots' official site reports. Per Mark Daniels of MassLive.com, Mike Vrabel said that the Patriots won't put a timeline on Henderson's return, while adding via Lazar that the team is "just trying to make sure that TreVeyon is cared for and his recovery plan is intact and he's comfortable with it." In the absence of Henderson's -- who recently experienced "an unexpected and unusual medical emergency involving a series of unexplained neurological symptoms" -- Rhamondre Stevenson will pace New England's backfield, with Corey Kiner and Lan Larison also mixing in.

items.head: Provides medical update Friday
items.body: In a statement posted to social media on Friday, Henderson -- who hasn't practiced since last Wednesday -- noted that he recently experienced "an unexpected and unusual medical emergency involving a series of unexplained neurological symptoms," Mike Reiss of ESPN reports. Henderson, who was unavailable for New England's Week 8 win over Miami, indicated that tests have "come back positive and reassuring," adding "I will continue working closely with specialists and physical therapists to focus on my recovery, as these symptoms have affected my strength, coordination, and some of my physical functions." The running back noted that for now he is "committed to doing everything necessary to return to full health" and that his "health and long-term well-being" remain his foremost priorities." In six games this season, while working in a Patriots backfield that also includes Rhamondre Stevenson, Corey Kiner and Lan Larison, Henderson has carried 52 times for 203 yar

items.head: Patriots' TreVeyon Henderson affected by neurological symptoms
items.body: Patriots RB TreVeyon Henderson said tests have come back positive after he suffered "unexplained neurological symptoms" that remain "unknown and unexplainable."

items.head: Not present Thursday
items.body: Henderson (illness) was not seen at Thursday's practice, Evan Lazar of the Patriots' official site reports. Henderson hasn't practiced since last Wednesday as he deals with an illness. Unless he returns to drills Thursday and/or Friday this week, he may be in danger of missing a second game in a row Sunday against the Packers. Thursday's injury report will reveal Henderson's activity level.

items.head: Won't practice Wednesday
items.body: Henderson (illness) won't practice Wednesday, Doug Kyed of the Boston Herald reports. Henderson also didn't practice this past Thursday and Friday, and then missed the Patriots' Week 8 win over the Dolphins. The running back's looming DNP suggests that he's no lock to play Sunday against the Packers, but Henderson's outlook on that front would no doubt improve with a return to the field in the next couple of days. In his absence against Miami, Rhamondre Stevenson paced New England's rushing attack, while Corey Kiner and Lan Larison mixed in.

items.head: Not available for Week 8
items.body: Henderson (illness) has been downgraded from questionable to out for Sunday's game against the Dolphins, Ian Rapoport of ESPN and NFL Network reports. Henderson was given the questionable tag for Week 8 despite missing the last two practices due to an illness. He won't travel with the team to Miami, so the Patriots' backfield will be led by Rhamondre Stevenson while Corey Kiner provides depth. Henderson's next opportunity to suit up is Week 9 against the Packers on Sunday, Nov. 8.

items.head: Questionable for Week 8
items.body: Henderson (illness) is questionable for Sunday's game against the Dolphins. Henderson logged DNPs on Thursday and Friday and appears to be in danger of missing Sunday's juicy matchup with Miami. His role has been shrinking of late anyway, and if Henderson misses this week's game, Rhamondre Stevenson and Corey Kiner will handle the backfield work for New England.

items.head: Will play Sunday
items.body: Fannin (groin) will play Sunday against the Saints, Daniel Oyefusi of ESPN.com reports. Coach Todd Monken said Fannin is "a little sore" but will be out there against New Orleans. On paper, it's a great spot for Fannin, but playing at less than 100 percent knocks him down a peg as a backend TE1 for fantasy.

items.head: Practicing Friday
items.body: Fannin (groin) is practicing Friday, Daniel Oyefusi of ESPN.com reports. After being listed as a limited participant Thursday, Fannin appears to be back on the field ahead of Sunday's game against the Saints. His Friday activity is a positive sign for his availability, but it doesn't confirm whether he'll carry an injury designation into the weekend.

items.head: Added to Week 9 injury report
items.body: Fannin (groin) was a limited participant in Thursday's practice, Scott Petrak of the Elyria Chronicle-Telegram reports. Fannin wasn't listed on Wednesday's injury report, so his appearance on it a day later is notable. It remains to be seen if Thursday's listed limitations were maintenance related or indicative of a setback, but the tight end may need to work fully Friday in order to approach Sunday's game against the Saints without an injury designation.

items.head: Harold Fannin Jr. (Groin) is Questionable
items.body: Fannin (groin) was a limited participant in Thursday's practice, Scott Petrak of the Elyria Chronicle-Telegram reports.

items.head: Career-best day in loss
items.body: Fannin brought in 10 of 12 targets for 154 yards in the Browns' 27-6 loss to the Steelers on Sunday. He also lost a fumble. Fannin was one of the few bright spots for the Browns on either side of the ball in the ugly loss despite an early fumble, setting new career highs in receptions, receiving yards and targets. Cleveland's gradual shift to a pass-centric approach as its deficit grew was a boon for Fannin's production, and the second-year tight end now has a combined 16-245-0 line on 21 targets over the last two games alone. Fannin will aim to carry over the elite caliber of play into a Week 9 road matchup against the Saints next Sunday.

items.head: Primed for key role sans Wilson
items.body: Cooper and Adonai Mitchell will be the Jets' top wide receivers with Garrett Wilson (concussion) unavailable for Sunday's game at Kansas City, ESPN's Rich Cimini reports. After back-to-back 100-yard games in his first two weeks off injured reserve, Cooper ran 26 routes last week without registering a target in the 38-33 loss to Las Vegas. Mitchell caught seven of nine targets for 142 yards and a touchdown, also running 26 routes, and Cimini's report notes that Mitchell "will become the No. 1 receiver" in Wilson's absence. Both Mitchell and Cooper figure to get plenty of snaps and routes, but targets and production aren't as assured.

items.head: No targets in Week 8
items.body: Cooper did not garner a target during Sunday's 38-33 loss to the Raiders. Cooper entered Week 8 having topped 100 receiving yards with a touchdown in back-to-back games, so Sunday's performance was especially disappointing. The rookie wideout was overshadowed by Adonai Mitchell (7-142-1) and Garrett Wilson (6-83-0) in the game, and it'll be hard to predict his workload ahead of the team's Week 9 matchup with the Chiefs.

items.head: A.J. Brown (Knee) is Out
items.body: Brown (knee) won't be available for Sunday's game against the Packers, Mark Daniels of Masslive.comreports.

items.head: Still not practicing
items.body: Brown (knee/ankle) remained sidelined at practice Friday, Doug Kyed of the Boston Herald reports. With three consecutive 'DNP's looming, Brown doesn't seem likely to be available Sunday against the Packers. If he's ruled out later Friday, the stage would be set for DeMario Douglas, Efton Chism, Kyle Williams and potentially Mack Hollins (calf) -- who has been designated to return from IR -- to handle New England's Week 9 WR duties.

items.head: A.J. Brown (Knee) is Questionable
items.body: Brown (ankle/knee) was a non-participant at Thursday's practice, Rob Demovsky of ESPN.com reports.

items.head: Absent again Thursday
items.body: Brown (ankle/knee) isn't present for the portion of Thursday's practice open to media viewing, Evan Lazar of the Patriots' official site reports. Brown appears set for a second straight missed practice after sitting out Wednesday's session on the heels of his absence during New England's Week 8 win over Miami. He'll have one more chance to practice Friday and will likely have to participate in some capacity to avoid being ruled out for Sunday's game against the Packers.

items.head: Set to miss Wednesday's practice
items.body: Brown (ankle/knee) won't practice Wednesday, Doug Kyed of the Boston Herald reports. Brown was sidelined for New England's Week 8 win over Miami, and with another 'DNP' - his third straight -- on tap, the wideout's status for Sunday's game against the Packers is cloudy. On the plus side for the Patriots, Mack Hollins (calf) could return from IR this weekend to bolster a WR corps that also includes DeMario Douglas, Efton Chism and Kyle Williams.

items.head: Practice participation this week TBD
items.body: When asked whether Brown (ankle/knee) might practice at some point this week, coach Mike Vrabel said Monday, "We'll see," Doug Kyed of the Boston Herald reports. Brown was inactive for Sunday's 24-19 win over the Dolphins, and Vrabel's comment Monday implies that the wideout's status for this weekend's game against the Packers is uncertain at this stage. In Brown's absence versus Miami, DeMario Douglas, Efton Chism and Kyle Williams paced the Patriots' Week 8 WR corps.

items.head: Won't play against Miami
items.body: Brown (knee/ankle) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Dolphins, Ian Rapoport of ESPN and NFL Network reports. Brown entered the weekend with the questionable tag despite being held out of practice both Thursday and Friday, and the knee injury that flared up during Wednesday's session is severe enough for the veteran wide receiver to miss Sunday's AFC East tilt. With Brown sidelined, the Patriots' pass-catching group will be led by DeMario Douglas, Efton Chism and tight end Hunter Henry. Brown's next opportunity to play is Week 9 against the Packers on Sunday, Nov. 8.

items.head: Listed as questionable for Week 8
items.body: Brown (ankle/knee) is questionable for Sunday's game at Miami, Evan Lazar of the Patriots' official site reports. Patriots coach Mike Vrabel deemed Brown questionable after Friday's practice, in which the wideout didn't participate. Vrabel told reporters that Brown's knee flared up during Wednesday's practice and prevented him from finishing the session, per Doug Kyed of the Boston Herald. Brown then missed practice Thursday and Friday, putting his availability in serious doubt ahead of a 4:25 p.m. ET kickoff at Miami on Sunday.

items.head: Set for RB1 work
items.body: With David Montgomery (groin) again ruled out for Week 9, Marks is expected to remain the Texans' clear RB1 for Sunday's game against the Chargers, Aaron Wilson of KPRC 2 Houston reports. Even with the Texans coming out of their bye week, Montgomery still isn't ready to return to the lineup. Additionally, Jawhar Jordan (quad) is also still out for Houston. With both backs sidelined in Week 7 against the Giants, Marks handled all 19 running-back carries for the Texans. The volume alone puts Marks in the RB1/2 conversation for fantasy this week.

items.head: Ready to play, ankle improving
items.body: Panthers coach Dave Canales said Friday that Young (ankle) is ready for Sunday's game against Denver after a "great week" of practice, Joe Person of The Athletic reports. Young has been a full practice participant throughout the week, apparently not too bothered by a sore ankle. The bigger concern for Sunday is Denver's impressive pass rush matching up against Carolina's injury-riddled offensive line.

Ian Rapoport of NFL Network previously suggested that Watson "is unlikely to start" Sunday's game against the Saints, but either way, the QB's return to the field, in any capacity, is a positive step toward him advancing through the NFL's concussion protocol. Friday's final injury report will add further clarity to Watson's Week 9 status, but if he isn't cleared to play this weekend, Shedeur Sanders would be in line to start in his place.

items.head: Unlikely to start Sunday
items.body: Watson (concussion) "is unlikely to start" Sunday's game against the Saints, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports. Watson has not practiced since being placed in the NFL's concussion protocol Tuesday, and it appears he will not be cleared to suit up for Week 9. The Browns will provide an official update on Watson's status later Friday, and if he is unable to go, Shedeur Sanders would presumably get the start in his place.

items.head: Deshaun Watson (Concussion) is Questionable
items.body: Watson (concussion) "is unlikely to start" Sunday's game against the Saints, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.

In the event that Watson doesn't gain clearance to play this weekend, Shedeur Sanders will draw the start in his place.

items.head: Unable to practice Wednesday
items.body: The Browns listed Watson (concussion) as a non-participant in Wednesday's practice. Early in this past Sunday's 27-6 loss to the Steelers, Watson exited the game to get checked for a concussion following a helmet-to-helmet hit, but he was cleared to re-enter the contest after missing just four offensive snaps. However, after he had some late-surfacing symptoms, Watson entered concussion protocol Tuesday and was a spectator for the Browns' first Week 9 session. According to Daniel Oyefusi of ESPN.com, Watson "felt a lot better" Wednesday and was involved in meetings, but Shedeur Sanders took all the reps with the first-team offense. items.head: Trending toward sitting out Week 9
items.body: Watson is expected to face an uphill battle to clear concussion protocol prior to Sunday's game against the Saints, leaving Shedeur Sanders as the Browns' likely Week 9 starting quarterback, Mary Kay Cabot of the Cleveland Plain Dealer reports. After reporting concussion symptoms Tuesday following Sunday's loss to the Steelers, Watson entered the protocol and isn't expected to practice Wednesday. Sanders will take all of the first-team reps Wednesday, and unless Watson can pass through the protocol quickly, the Browns will prepare for the second-year signal-caller to direct the offense in Week 9.

items.head: Placed in concussion protocol
items.body: The Browns announced Wednesday that Watson has been placed in concussion protocol. Watson took a helmet-to-helmet hit in the first quarter of Sunday's 27-6 loss to the Steelers, and after being examined by an independent consultant he was cleared to return to the game. Though subsequent tests after the game and Monday morning showed no symptoms of a concussion, Watson informed the Browns on Tuesday morning that he was experiencing symptoms and was "immediately placed in the concussion protocol," per the team. Watson will need to clear the five-step protocol in order to play in Cleveland's Week 9 matchup with New Orleans, but if he's unable to go, Shedeur Sanders would be in line to start at quarterback for the first time this season.

items.head: Over 300 passing yards in loss
items.body: Watson completed 27 of 39 passes for 324 yards with no touchdowns or interceptions while rushing three times for two yards in the Browns' 27-6 loss to the Steelers on Sunday. He also lost a fumble. Watson couldn't lead the Browns to a single touchdown, but he exceeded 300 passing yards for the second straight game since Cleveland was forced into a pass-centric approach. Watson displayed the most chemistry with Harold Fannin (10-154-0 on 12 targets), and he recorded completions to seven different targets overall. Watson also lost the handle on a combined sack by Patrick Queen and Cameron Heyward in the first quarter, which led to a Steelers touchdown. Watson will look to rebound in a favorable road matchup against the Saints in Week 9 next Sunday.

items.head: Emeka Egbuka (Foot) is Questionable
items.body: Buccaneers coach Todd Bowles said Friday that Egbuka (foot) will be a game-time decision for Sunday night's game against the Bears, Greg Auman of Fox Sports reports.

items.head: Looks ready for Sunday
items.body: Egbuka (foot) has been "full go" at practice and doesn't appear to have had any setbacks ahead of Sunday's matchup with the Bears, Greg Auman of Fox Sports reports. With Egbuka having logged a full practice Thursday and seemingly repeating that Friday morning, he appears ready to return from a two-game absence. He should handle his usual workload in a matchup between two of the NFC's hottest teams Sunday night.

items.head: Upgrades to full practice
items.body: Egbuka (foot) was a full participant in Thursday's practice, Scott Smith of the Buccaneers' official site reports. After missing Wednesday's practice, Egbuka was back in the mix in full on Thursday. The second-year wideout has missed the last two games due to a concussion and a foot injury, but appears to be on track to return Sunday in Chicago. Getting Egbuka back in the fold would be a boon for a Buccaneers' passing game which has yet to hit its stride this season.

items.head: Back at practice Thursday
items.body: Egbuka, who was present for practice Thursday, was spotted testing his injured foot, Greg Auman of Fox Sports reports. While Egbuka opened up the practice week with a DNP on Wednesday,  Auman relays that the wideout was running full speed on the side during that session. The Buccaneers' upcoming official practice report will reveal the official Thursday participation level of Egbuka, who last saw game action in Week 6.

items.head: Doesn't practice Wednesday
items.body: Head coach Todd Bowles said Egbuka (foot) didn't practice Wednesday, but the wide receiver was able to run on a side field, and the Buccaneers will see how he feels Thursday, Scott Smith of the Buccaneers' official site reports. Egbuka was able to clear ths concussion protocol last Friday, but he still missed this past Sunday's win against the Falcons due to a foot injury, marking a second absence in a row. Seemingly, Wednesday's bit of running is a test to get a sense of where Egbuka stands, health-wise, so Thursday's session could be revealing for his chances to return to action Sunday at Chicago.

items.head: Works on the side Wednesday
items.body: Egbuka (foot) was spotted running on the side with a trainer Wednesday, Greg Auman of Fox Sports reports. Egbuka, who last suited up for game action in Week 6, was limited at practice last Wednesday and Thursday before logging a DNP on Friday. It remains to be seen what his participation level will be as the week unfolds, but if Egbuka remains sidelined Sunday night against the Bears, Chris Godwin, Ted Hurst and Tez Johnson would be in line to lead Tampa Bay's Week 9 WR corps.

items.head: Two grabs in another blowout win
items.body: Strange caught both of his targets for 22 yards in Thursday night's 33-10 win over the Ravens. The Jaguars keep blowing teams out and aren't being pushed on offense, which is keeping Trevor Lawrence's pass volume low. Strange is still making the most of his few opportunities, totaling four grabs for 77 yards on four targets over the last two weeks, games in which the Jaguars have combined to outscore their opponents 75-17. Strange is a TE1 for fantasy and gets a date with the Titans in nine days.

items.head: Two snags in blowout victory
items.body: Strange caught both of his targets for 55 yards during Sunday's 42-7 win over Indianapolis. Strange was able to make it seven games in a row with multiple catches to open the 2026 campaign. The tight end tied running back Bhayshul Tuten for the team lead in receiving yards, exceeding 50 yards for the third time in the last four games. Strange has now reeled in 28 of 35 targets for 334 yards and a touchdown over seven contests this season.

items.head: Present for Friday's practice
items.body: Henry (foot) is present for the media-access portion of Friday's practice, Mike Reiss of ESPN.com reports. After missing practice both Wednesday and Thursday, Henry's presence for Friday's session is a positive sign ahead of Sunday's game against the Packers. The Patriots' upcoming injury report will reveal both the tight end's official participation level, as well as his Week 9 game status.

items.head: Absent again Thursday
items.body: Henry (foot) wasn't spotted at Thursday's practice, Evan Lazar of the Patriots' official site reports. Henry has started Week 9 prep with back-to-back absences after exiting during the Patriots' Week 8 win over Miami. If the veteran tight end is unable to practice in at least some capacity Friday, he'll likely be ruled out for Sunday's game against the Packers, paving the way for rookie third-round pick Eli Raridon to take on an expanded role.

items.head: Sitting out first practice of Week 9
items.body: Henry (foot) wasn't on the field for the media-access portion of Wednesday's practice, Mike Reiss of ESPN.com reports. Henry was unable to return to Sunday's 24-19 win over the Dolphins after exiting in the second quarter due to the foot issue. The Patriots haven't provided many details regarding the severity of the injury, but Henry will be sidelined as the team begins Week 9 prep. Henry will have two more chances to potentially practice this week before the Patriots decide whether he'll take a designation into Sunday's game against the Packers.

items.head: Status uncertain for Week 9
items.body: Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel said Monday that he had no update on Henry's (foot) status heading into Sunday's game against the Packers, Karen Guregian of MassLive.com reports. "I don't have any expectations yet," Vrabel said of Henry. "It's kind of how he responds here. He wasn't able to finish the [Week 8] game. So we'll see where he is, and I know Hunter will do everything he can to get back to help us." Henry recorded three receptions for 30 yards on three targets before exiting in the second quarter of Sunday's 24-19 win over the Dolphins due to the foot issue. The Patriots haven't provided any further word on where exactly Henry stands in his recovery, but more context on that front should arrive when the team releases its first Week 9 injury report Wednesday. Despite his early departure in Week 8, Henry leads the team in receptions (29) and is second to only wideout DeMario Douglas in receiving yards (326) through eight games.

items.head: Won't return Sunday
items.body: Henry (foot) has been ruled out for the rest of Sunday's game in Miami. Henry exited in the first half of this Week 8 matchup and eventually was ruled out midway through the fourth quarter. He ended with three catches (on three targets) for 30 yards. Eli Raridon will act as the Patriots' top pass-catching tight end for as long as Henry is sidelined.

items.head: Questionable to return Sunday
items.body: Henry (foot) is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Dolphins. Prior to his departure from the contest, Henry had caught all three of his targets for 30 yards. Next up for the Patriots' TE snaps in his absence is Eli Raridon, with Cameron Latu and Tanner Arkin also on hand versus Miami.

items.head: Not targeted in Week 9 win
items.body: Thomas wasn't targeted in Thursday night's 33-10 win over the Ravens. Thomas played just 19 of 56 offensive snaps and ran only 11 routes on Trevor Lawrence's 26 dropbacks. It's become clear that Thomas is no longer a big part of the offense and needs an injury ahead of him or a trade out of Jacksonville to become relevant in season-long fantasy. He has just one catch for a 12-yard touchdown over his last four games.

items.head: Appealing trade target for number of teams
items.body: Thomas "has been the area of interest for a lot of other teams" leading up to the Nov. 10 trade deadline, Ian Rapoport of ESPN reports. Since delivering an 87-1,282-10 receiving line over 17 games as a rookie in 2024, Thomas' production has cratered in the ensuing two seasons. He's been firmly behind fellow wideouts Parker Washington and Jakobi Meyers (hamstring/ankle) in terms of snap share through the Jaguars' first seven games of 2026 and has drawn more than three targets in just one of those contests. Though the vertical threat Thomas presents makes him an appealing target for teams seeking a big-play receiver ahead of the deadline, Rapoport acknowledges that it's unclear if the Jaguars have much motivation to move him. Despite his declining role within the Jacksonville offense, Thomas remains under contract through next

items.head: Snags red-zone TD in easy win
items.body: Thomas caught one of two targets for a 12-yard touchdown in Sunday's 42-7 win over the Colts. Thomas got the scoring started against Indianapolis, securing a red-zone touchdown with 5:30 left in the opening quarter. With the Jaguars throttling the Colts, Trevor Lawrence dropped back just 17 times all afternoon. On 17 pass attempts between Lawrence (14) and Quinn Ewers (three), 11 different Jaguars drew at least one target. Through seven games this season, Thomas has 10 catches for 117 yards and two touchdowns on 22 targets. A low catch rate and diminished snaps have led to Thomas' name being circulated in trade rumors 10 days ahead of the trade deadline.

items.head: Garrett Wilson (Concussion) is Out
items.body: Wilson (concussion) is out for Sunday's game against the Chiefs, Brian Costello of the New York Post reports.

items.head: Not spotted at practice Thursday
items.body: Wilson, who is in the NFL's concussion protocol, wasn't seen at Thursday's practice, Antwan Staley of the New York Daily News reports. Wilson also logged a DNP on Wednesday, so the wideout's apparent absence from Thursday's session sets the stage for Friday's practice to loom large in terms of his availability for Sunday's game against the Chiefs. In the event that Wilson isn't cleared to play, added targets will be available for some combo of WRs Omar Cooper, Adonai Mitchell and Isaiah Williams, as well as tight ends Mason Taylor (back) and Kenyon Sadiq.

items.head: Enters concussion protocol, day-to-day
items.body: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said that Wilson is in the NFL's concussion protocol and is considered day-to-day,  Zack Rosenblatt of The Athletic reports. Per Eric Allen of the Jets' official site, Wilson experienced symptoms of a concussion when he was evaluated Monday after taking a hard hit near the end of Sunday's 38-33 loss to the Jets.  As a result, Wilson won't practice Wednesday, and his status for Sunday's road game against the Chiefs will need to be tracked closely in the coming days. If Wilson ends up being sidelined this weekend, added targets could be available for wideouts Omar Cooper, Adonai Mitchell and Isaiah Williams and tight ends Mason Taylor and Kenyon Sadiq.

items.head: Targeted 12 times in Week 8 loss
items.body: Wilson caught six of 12 targets for 83 yards in Sunday's 38-33 loss to the Raiders. Wilson saw his second-highest target total of the season Sunday after being targeted a season-low three times in the Week 7 loss to Miami. After being outplayed by Omar Cooper in each of the previous two games, Wilson took a back seat to Adonai Mitchell in this one, as Mitchell caught seven of nine targets for 142 yards and a touchdown while Cooper went without a target. The Jets have three capable wide receivers for the first time in a while, but Wilson easily leads the team with 527 receiving yards heading into a Week 9 road game against the Chiefs, while Mitchell's a distant second with 265 receiving yards.

items.head: Will practice Friday
items.body: Wright (quadriceps) will practice Friday, Barry Jackson of the Miami Herald reports. Averaging a miserable 1.9 yards per carry this season, Wright has no fantasy appeal other than being Ollie Gordon's ineffective backup.

items.head: Jaylen Wright (Quadriceps) is Questionable
items.body: Wright (quadriceps) will practice Friday, Barry Jackson of the Miami Herald reports.

items.head: Limited Thursday
items.body: Wright (quadriceps) was limited in Thursday's practice, Marcel Louis-Jacques of ESPN.com reports. Wright has been battling various issues all season and hasn't been effective when on the field, yet he's still operating as the Dolphins' lightly-used RB2 behind Ollie Gordon. Wright is averaging a microscopic 1.9 yards per carry this season.

items.head: Returns to practice Thursday
items.body: Wright (quadriceps) is taking part in practice Thursday, David Furones of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports. Wright didn't practice Wednesday, so Thursday's practice appearance is a step in the right direction, but the extent of his participation remains to be seen. Ollie Gordon has cemented himself as the lead back for the Dolphins, while Wright hasn't exceeded six touches in a game this season.

items.head: Sits out first Week 9 practice
items.body: Wright (quadriceps) was a non-participant in Wednesday's practice, David Furones of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports. In addition to a foot injury, Wright was listed with the same quad issue on the Dolphins' Week 8 injury report but proceeded to log three full practices before playing in Sunday's 24-19 loss to the Patriots. Though he played just 13 total snaps between offense and special teams in Week 8, Wright apparently emerged from the contest with his quad injury still bothering him. He'll have two more chances to get back to full practice participation prior to this Sunday's game against the Lions.

items.head: Remains non-factor in Week 8
items.body: Wright rushed two times for five yards in Sunday's 24-19 loss to the Patriots. Wright failed to catch his lone target in the passing game and remains firmly planted behind Ollie Gordon on the depth chart. While Gordon has been one of the most productive running backs on a per-carry basis this season, Wright has seemingly been stuck in the mud as a runner, averaging a pitiful 1.9 yards per carry on 22 attempts.

items.head: Could practice Friday
items.body: Head coach Brian Schottenheimer hopes that Ferguson (ankle) will be "back on the field" Friday, Tommy Yarrish of the Cowboys' official site reports. Ferguson did not get any work in Wednesday or Thursday due to the ankle injury he sustained in Week 8, but it appears there is a chance he could practice in some capacity Friday. The Cowboys will reveal his official status for Week 9 at some point following the conclusion of Friday's session.

items.head: Jake Ferguson (Ankle) is Questionable
items.body: Head coach Brian Schottenheimer hopes that Ferguson (ankle) will be "back on the field" Friday, Tommy Yarrish of the Cowboys' official site reports.

items.head: Remains unavailable Thursday
items.body: Ferguson (ankle) did not practice Thursday, Todd Archer of ESPN.com reports. Ferguson's back-to-back absences to kick off Week 9 prep don't bode well for his availability Sunday against the Colts. He sustained a low-ankle sprain after playing just four snaps during Dallas' Week 8 loss to the Cardinals. Brevyn Spann-Ford worked as the team's top TE after Ferguson's exit. Ferguson will have one more opportunity to practice Friday before Dallas posts Week 9 game statuses.

items.head: Officially unavailable for practice
items.body: Ferguson (ankle) did not participate at the Cowboys' practice Wednesday, Patrik Walker of the team's official site reports. As expected, Ferguson was unavailable for practice as he worked off to the side with the team's training staff. The tight end is working through a low-ankle sprain that he suffered during the team's 33-30 overtime loss to Arizona in Week 8, and his availability for Sunday's matchup against the Colts is in question. Ferguson will have two more chances to return to practice this week, but if he can't go for Week 9, Brevyn Spann-Ford would be a top candidate to take over as the primary tight end for Dallas.

items.head: Working with trainers Wednesday
items.body: Head coach Brian Schottenheimer said Ferguson (ankle) will work with the Cowboys' training staff during Wednesday's practice, Briana Aldridge of CBS News Texas reports. Such comments are an indication that Ferguson will go down as a DNP to kick off Week 9 prep, something that'll be revealed on Wednesday's injury report. Ferguson is tending to a low-ankle sprain in the wake of this past Sunday's loss to the Cardinals.

items.head: Has chance to play Sunday
items.body: Head coach Brian Schottenheimer said Monday that Ferguson (ankle) has a chance to play Sunday at Indianapolis, Jon Machota of The Athletic reports. Ferguson hurt his ankle early in Sunday's eventual overtime loss to the Cardinals, eventually was ruled out and then diagnosed with a low-ankle sprain. Schottenheimer's comments one day later follow the general belief that players often are able to gut out such injuries, but how Ferguson fares in practice Wednesday through Friday will determine his availability for Week 9.

items.head: Sustains low-ankle sprain
items.body: Ferguson suffered a low-ankle sprain during Sunday's loss to the Cardinals, Jeremy Fowler of ESPN reports. Ferguson picked up an ankle injury on the Cowboys' first drive of the game and eventually was ruled out after halftime. He thus finished Week 8 without a target, making it his second contest in a row with no catches in the box score. Low-ankle sprains typically can be played through, but Ferguson's status will be watched to get a sense of his potential to suit up next Sunday at Indianapolis.

items.head: Ruled out for rest of game
items.body: Ferguson (ankle) won't return to Sunday's game against the Cardinals, Joe Hoyt reports. Prior to his exit, Ferguson wasn't targeted by QB Dak Prescott. In his absence versus Arizona, Brevyn Spann-Ford and James Mitchell are available to handle TE duties for the remainder of Sunday's contest.

items.head: Will remain limited Friday
items.body: Pickens (hamstring) "will be a little bit limited" Friday, but head coach Brian Schottenheimer is "hopeful" he will play Sunday against the Colts, Tommy Yarrish of the Cowboys' official site reports. Pickens was limited at practice both Wednesday and Thursday due to a hamstring issue, and it appears he will find himself in a similar spot at Friday's practice. The Cowboys will provide another update on his status after the latest session comes to a close.

items.head: George Pickens (Hamstring) is Questionable
items.body: Pickens (hamstring) "will be a little bit limited" Friday, but head coach Brian Schottenheimer is "hopeful" he will play Sunday against the Colts, Tommy Yarrish of the Cowboys' official site reports.

items.head: Another limited session
items.body: Pickens (hamstring) was limited at Thursday's practice, Todd Archer of ESPN.com reports. Pickens maintained his activity level from Wednesday as he deals with lingering shoulder and hamstring injuries. He still was able to handle a 57 percent snap share this past Sunday against the Cardinals, but he mustered only two catches (on four targets) for 48 yards. Friday's practice report will unveil whether or not Pickens heads into the weekend with a designation for Sunday's game at Indianapolis.

items.head: Limited in Wednesday's practice
items.body: Pickens (hamstring) was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice, Patrik Walker of the Cowboys' official site reports. Pickens was limited by shoulder and hamstring injuries last week, but he was able to suit up this past Sunday against the Cardinals, logging a 57 percent snap share and gathering in two of four targets for 48 yards. As Week 9 prep kicks off, he's being listed with only the hamstring issue, which continues to impact his on-field work. Pickens will have two more chances to get back to full Thursday and Friday before Dallas potentially tags him with a designation for Sunday's contest at Indianapolis.

items.head: Only two receptions in Week 8
items.body: Pickens tallied two catches (on four targets) for 48 yards during Sunday's 33-30 overtime loss to the Cardinals. Pickens' inconsistency from week to week in 2026 continued in Week 8, as he matched his season low in receptions and ended up with his third-fewest receiving yards in a contest through the first eight games. Granted, his activity level was limited Wednesday through Friday due to shoulder and hamstring injuries, so he was operating at less than 100 percent health-wise Sunday. In any case, Pickens will strive for better results next Sunday on the road against the Colts.

items.head: Active for Sunday's game
items.body: Pickens (shoulder/hamstring) is listed as active Sunday against the Cardinals. Pickens played through a shoulder issue in Week 7, but a hamstring injury was added to the Cowboys' practice report this week, limiting him on the field Wednesday through Friday and resulting in a questionable designation ahead of Sunday's matchup. Adam Schefter of ESPN reported Sunday morning that Pickens is expected to play in Week 8, which now has been confirmed. With a 37-485-2 line on 58 targets through seven contests this season, Pickens has been playing second fiddle to fellow WR CeeDee Lamb (53-651-6 on 81 targets in seven appearances) in the passing game, but the former's output still has been more than useful from a fantasy standpoint.

items.head: Slated to suit up Sunday
items.body: Pickens (shoulder/hamstring) is expected to play Sunday against the Cardinals, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports. Pickens was limited by dueling shoulder and hamstring injuries during the entirety of Week 8 prep, but he appears as if he'll avoid the Cowboys' inactive list approximately 90 minutes before Sunday's 1:00 p.m. kickoff. He's so far put together a 37-485-2 line on 58 targets through the first seven contests of the campaign.

items.head: Questionable for Sunday
items.body: Pickens (shoulder/hamstring) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Cardinals, Patrik Walker of the Cowboys' official site reports. Pickens was listed as limited on all three of the Cowboys' Week 8 practice reports due to a lingering shoulder injury and a new hamstring issue, leaving his status up in the air heading into the weekend. His availability, or lack thereof, will be clarified about 90 minutes before Sunday's 1:00 p.m. ET kickoff.

items.head: Expected to play Sunday
items.body: Hall (quadriceps) "has been medically cleared" and is expected to play Sunday against the Chiefs, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports. Hall has not taken the field since sustaining a quad injury in Week 3, but he practiced fully Thursday and appears primed to return to action Sunday. Braelon Allen has shined in Hall's absence, but Hall entered the season as the starter, so both figure to be involved to some degree in Week 9.

items.head: Practices fully Thursday
items.body: Hall (quadriceps) was a full participant in Thursday's practice. After opening the week with a limited session, Hall upgraded to full participation Thursday, indicating that he's in the clear to return Sunday against the Chiefs for his first action since Week 3. Braelon Allen has thrived in the lead role during Hall's absence, and offensive coordinator Frank Reich said Thursday that the Jets intend to utilize "a mix" of the two running backs Sunday, per Al Iannazzone of Newsday Sports. Hall is the superior receiving back, but Allen is averaging 5.0 yards per carry while Hall averaged just 3.2 YPC prior to getting hurt.

items.head: Says he's ready to go this week
items.body: Hall (quadriceps) indicated Thursday that he's ready to play Sunday against the Chiefs, Rich Cimini of ESPN.com reports. Hall, who hasn't played since Sept. 27, participated in Thursday's practice, though it remains to be seen if the Jets list him as a full or limited participant. In any case, the running back is trending toward a return to action this weekend, and if he is indeed available versus Kansas City, Hall will rejoin a backfield that's been capably paced paced by Braelon Allen in his absence.

items.head: Practicing again Thursday
items.body: Hall (quadriceps) is participating in Thursday's practice, Rich Cimini of ESPN.com reports. Hall, who was a limited participant at Wednesday's practice session, was also limited throughout the week leading up to the Jets' Week 8 loss to the Raiders, which the running back sat out. While the team's coaching staff has expressed optimism that Hall will be ready to return Sunday against the Chiefs, his status will remain up in the air until he's able to practice without limitations. Thursday's participation level has yet to be revealed, but Hall's presence at practice suggests that he has at least avoided a setback.

items.head: Set for limited practice Wednesday
items.body: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said that Hall (quadriceps) will be a limited practice participant Wednesday, Zack Rosenblatt of The Athletic reports. Hall, who hasn't played since Sept. 27, was also limited at practice last week, but Glenn said that the running back is "trending in the right direction" as Sunday's game against the Chiefs approaches, per Rich Cimini of ESPN.com. As for how the workload might be split between Hall and Braelon Allen should Hall return this weekend, Glenn declined to go in specifics beyond noting that "both will play" in such a scenario, according to Cimini.

items.head: Expected back for Week 9
items.body: Hall (quadriceps) is considered "good to go" and is expected to return to action in next Sunday's game against the Chiefs, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports. Though he was sidelined for a fifth straight game in Sunday's 38-33 loss to the Raiders, Hall displayed progress in his recovery from a right quad injury by practicing on a limited practice participant throughout Week 8 prep. As long as he's able to upgrade to full activity at some point during Week 9, Hall should get the green light to play in Kansas City, but he may not be guaranteed a full workload while backup Braelon Allen has likely earned himself more opportunities by averaging 114.8 scrimmage yards per game in Hall's absence over the last five contests.

items.head: Inactive for Sunday's game
items.body: Hall (quadriceps) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Raiders. Hall practiced on a limited basis Wednesday through Friday, but it was reported earlier Sunday that he was not expected to suit up for Week 8, and he will indeed miss a fifth straight game. The Jets are reportedly hoping Hall will return in Week 9, but for at least one more week, Braelon Allen will be New York's primary running back and Isaiah Davis will occupy the No. 2 spot.

items.head: Not expected to play Sunday
items.body: Hall (quadriceps), who is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Raiders, isn't expected to play, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports. Though Hall was able to practice in a limited fashion from Wednesday through Friday, the Jets presumably want to see him log a full session before clearing him for game action. Per Jeremy Fowler of ESPN.com, the Jets are "hoping for next week" for Hall's return, so expect him to be officially ruled out for a fifth consecutive contest when the team releases its inactive list 90 minutes prior to Sunday's 1 p.m. ET kickoff. Braelon Allen is slated to make another start in place of the banged-up Hall.

items.head: Brian Robinson Jr. (Hamstring) is Out
items.body: Robinson (hamstring) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Bengals, Tori McElhaney of the Falcons' official site reports.

items.head: Limited at practice Thursday
items.body: Robinson (hamstring) was a limited participant in Thursday's practice, Tori McElhaney of the Falcons' official site reports. Robinson also was deemed limited on Wednesday's estimated injury report, which gives the running back one more opportunity to upgrade to full participation before the team assigns Week 9 injury designations. If he's able to return from a two-game absence Sunday against the Bengals, he'd slot back into a complementary role behind Bijan Robinson, an assignment that Khalil Herbert handled in Weeks 7 and 8.

items.head: Opens week with limited practice
items.body: The Falcons listed Robinson (hamstring) as a limited participant on Wednesday's estimated practice report, Tori McElhaney of the team's official site reports. After landing in Spain early Wednesday in advance of Sunday's game versus the Bengals in Madrid, the Falcons opted to hold a walkthrough rather than a traditional practice. Robinson was able to do enough to garner a limited listing on the injury report, marking the first time since Week 7 that he's gone down as anything other than a non-participant in practice. If Robinson can get back to full activity Thursday or Friday, he'll put himself on track to be available as the top complement to lead back Bijan Robinson on Sunday.

items.head: Won't play Sunday
items.body: Robinson (hamstring) has been ruled out for Sunday's game at Tampa Bay, Will McFadden of the Falcons' official site reports. After being listed as a non-participant on five straight injury reports due to a hamstring issue, Robinson will miss a second consecutive contest. In Robinson's absence, Khalil Herbert will continue to serve as the No. 2 RB to Bijan Robinson.

items.head: Another DNP on Friday
items.body: Robinson (hamstring) remained sidelined for Friday's practice, Josh Kendall of The Athletic reports. Robinson looks likely to miss a second straight game, as he's yet to return to practice. Khalil Herbert should once again handle RB2 duties behind Bijan Robinson on Sunday against the Bucs.

items.head: Ravens refuse to blame historic rut on loss of Lamar Jackson
items.body: The Ravens say one of the worst stretches in team history cannot be pinned on the loss of the injured Lamar Jackson.

items.head: Will have surgery and go on IR
items.body: Jackson is slated to have surgery to address his right thumb injury and will be placed on injured reserve, per coach Jesse Minter,  Brian Wacker of The Baltimore Sun reports. Wacker also notes that Jackson's injury could potentially be season-ending according to Minter, with more context on that front presumably slated to arrive after the QB's thumb is checked out further. With Tyler Huntley dealing with a toe injury, Baltimore's QB situation is in flux in Week 9, and beyond. Joe Fagnano finished up Sunday's game against the Bills, and it's likely the Ravens will add signal-caller depth ahead of Thursday's game against the Jaguars.

items.head: Ruled out for rest of Sunday's game
items.body: Jackson (right thumb) has been ruled out for the remainder of Sunday's game against the Bills. After previously being deemed questionable to return, Jackson has now been confirmed to be unavailable for the rest of the contest. In his absence, Tyler Huntley has taken over the Ravens' QB duties versus Buffalo. Prior to his first-quarter exit, Jackson didn't complete his only passing attempt.

items.head: Questionable to return with thumb injury
items.body: Jackson is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Bills due to a right thumb injury. Jackson remains in the Baltimore locker room for further evaluation after he was forced out of the game following the team's first offensive play of the day, when his hand made contact with a Bills defender as he was following through on a throw. Tyler Huntley took over at quarterback and will be tasked with directing the offense for the rest of the afternoon if Jackson is unable to return. Jackson had been cleared to start Sunday after missing the Ravens' previous three games due to an ankle sprain.

items.head: Hurts hand during opening drive
items.body: Jackson headed to the locker room after sustaining an apparent injury to his throwing hand during Sunday's game against the Bills, Jonas Shaffer of TheBaltimoreBanner.com reports. After missing the Ravens' previous three games due to an ankle sprain, Jackson lasted just one play before succumbing to a new injury. The quarterback was in visible pain after his hand appeared to make contact with the arm of a Bills defender while he was following through on a pass attempt. Rather than heading to the medical tent on the sideline, Jackson immediately jogged to the locker room to receive treatment. Until the Ravens provide an update on Jackson's status, Tyler Huntley will direct the offense.

items.head: Will play Sunday
items.body: Ravens coach Jesse Minter confirmed Friday that Jackson (ankle) will play in Sunday's game at Buffalo, Brian Wacker of The Baltimore Sun reports. This outcome was likely once the Ravens listed Jackson as a full practice participant Wednesday and Thursday. It's possible he won't be at his best as a runner after missing three games with a high-ankle sprain, although he told reporters Friday that lingering pain in the ankle shouldn't impact his movement.

items.head: Late rushing TD in win
items.body: Rodriguez rushed 10 times for 19 yards and a touchdown and brought in both targets for 13 yards in the Jaguars' 33-10 win over the Ravens on Thursday night. Rodriguez finished with just two fewer carries than Bhayshul Tuten, who came into the game managing ankle and foot injuries and was able to log a relatively abbreviated workload thanks to game script. Both backs had plenty of trouble against Baltimore's stout run defense, but Rodriguez salvaged his fantasy night with a two-yard TD run just past the midway point of the fourth quarter. Rodriguez now has scored in back-to-back games heading into a Week 10 road matchup against the Titans on Sunday, Nov. 15.

items.head: No Week 9 injury designation
items.body: Rodriguez (hand) doesn't carry an injury designation for Thursday night's game against the Ravens. Meanwhile, Bhayshul Tuten (ankle/foot) has been deemed questionable for the contest after being listed as a DNP on each of the Jaguars' injury reports, Monday through Wednesday. Given that Tuten has been the team's lead back this season, his playing status (and potential workload, if he's active Thursday) will provide valuable context related to the Week 9 fantasy prospects of Rodriguez, who could assume a larger backfield role versus Baltimore if Tuten ends up out or limited.

items.head: Limited in Tuesday's practice
items.body: Rodriguez (hand) was listed as a limited participant in Tuesday's practice. Though he's been deemed a limited participant on both of the Jaguars' first two Week 9 practice reports, Rodriguez still looks to be in a better spot on the health front than Bhayshul Tuten (ankle/foot), who has yet to log any practice activity. If Tuten winds up being sidelined for Thursday's game in Baltimore, Rodriguez would be the favorite to lead the Jacksonville ground attack, provided he's not inhibited by his own hand injury.

items.head: Tending to hand injury
items.body: Rodriguez was listed as limited on Monday's practice estimate due to a hand injury. The Jaguars listed two running backs on their first Week 9 injury report, with No. 1 option Bhayshul Tuten (ankle/foot) going down as a non-participant. There's no telling if Tuten is in danger of missing Thursday's contest at Baltimore, but Rodriguez could be in line for more early down work if he's active and the former is inhibited or sidelined. On the season, Rodriguez is averaging 6.7 touches per game.

items.head: Reaches end zone in blowout win
items.body: Rodriguez registered 41 yards and a touchdown on six carries while reeling in his only target for 17 yards during Sunday's 42-7 win over the Colts. Rodriguez was able to exceed 40 rushing yards for the second straight game after failing to do so in any of the team's first five contests of the year. Additionally, the running back slashed through the Colts' defense for a 26-yard touchdown in the third quarter, reaching the end zone for the third time this season. Rodriguez has now rushed 45 times for 209 yards and three scores while reeling in one of two targets for six yards over seven contests so far during the 2026 campaign.

items.head: Season-high rushing yardage total
items.body: Hill rushed nine times for 85 yards and a touchdown and brought in all three targets for seven yards in the Ravens' 33-10 loss to the Jaguars on Thursday night. Hill provided the sole offensive highlight of the night for the moribund, Joe Fagnano-led offense, making one cut after getting the handoff from the rookie quarterback halfway through the fourth quarter and bursting through the defense up the right side of the field for a 65-yard touchdown run. Hill's yardage total was both a team- and season-high figure for the veteran change-of-pace back, who should benefit from the pending trade acquisition of Jacoby Brissett from the Cardinals whenever the veteran signal-caller is able to take the reins of the offense.

items.head: Churns out full practice
items.body: Hill (groin) was a full participant in Tuesday's practice. After the Ravens estimated him as a limited practice participant Monday on their initial Week 9 injury report, Hill took every rep Tuesday to clear up any concern about his availability heading into Thursday's game against the Jaguars. Hill should serve in his familiar role as the Ravens' top passing-down back in Week 9, with Derrick Henry continuing to lead the way on the ground.

items.head: Estimated as limited Monday
items.body: Hill (groin) was estimated as a limited participant on Monday's practice report. It's a new injury for Hill, as it's the first time this season he's been listed on the injury report. In Sunday's loss to the Bills, Hill rushed three times for 15 yards and posted season highs in catches (four) and targets (eight) for 20 receiving yards.

items.head: Leads team in catches in loss
items.body: Hill rushed three times for 15 yards while catching four of eight targets for 20 yards during Sunday's 36-10 loss to the Bills. Hill garnered a team-high eight targets as Baltimore saw the departure of both starting quarterback Lamar Jackson (thumb) and Tyler Huntley (toe) in the first half. Undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano completed 10 of 21 passes for 91 yards while throwing an interception in the loss, and he may be asked to start Thursday's contest against the Jaguars. Hill has now turned 24 carries into 155 yards while reeling in 17 of 25 targets for 104 yards over eight games to open the 2026 campaign.

items.head: Two catches in Week 9 loss
items.body: Andrews secured both targets for 19 yards in the Ravens' 33-10 loss to the Jaguars on Thursday night. The veteran tight end actually led the Ravens in receiving yards with his modest total, as fill-in signal-caller Joe Fagnano averaged just 3.3 yards per attempt and totaled 60 passing yards overall. Andrews opened the season with back-to-back 49-yard tallies on 10 total catches, but he's been stuck at 28 receiving yards or fewer in his seven subsequent games. Andrews will hope to benefit from the pending trade acquisition of Jacoby Brissett, who should bring some stability and productivity to Baltimore's currently embattled quarterback situation.

items.head: Three grabs amid QB issues
items.body: Andrews caught three of four targets for 14 yards in Sunday's 36-10 loss to the Bills. Though Lamar Jackson (ankle) made his long-awaited return to the lineup, his stay lasted just one offensive snap Sunday before he suffered a serious thumb injury. Tyler Huntley then exited the game with a toe injury in the second quarter, forcing undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano into emergency QB duties. No Ravens player produced even 25 receiving yards against Buffalo. Andrews has been in an extended slump and won't be a trustworthy fantasy tight end for Thursday night against the Jaguars.

items.head: Modest numbers in starting role
items.body: Fagnano completed 10 of 18 passes for 60 yards with no touchdowns and two interceptions while adding three rushes for 13 yards in the Ravens' 33-10 loss to the Jaguars on Thursday night. Fagnano drew the start with both Lamar Jackson (thumb) and Tyler Huntley (toe) on injured reserve, and the undrafted rookie signal-caller unsurprisingly had a difficult night after also struggling in emergency duty against the Bills just four days earlier. Fagnano had been dealing with an ankle injury stemming from his aforementioned NFL debut and had little practice time on a short week, so offensive coordinator Declan Doyle kept the game plan simple and focused on the short areas of the field, resulting in Fagnano averaging just 3.3 yards per attempt. Both of Fagnano's second-half picks also led to Jacksonville field goals, making it a forgettable night overall. With the Ravens reportedly

items.head: Still in line to start Thursday
items.body: Trade acquisition Jacoby Brissett is not expected to be available for Baltimore until Week 10, leaving Fagnano as the team's projected starting quarterback for Week 9, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports. With Lamar Jackson bound for IR with a thumb injury to his throwing hand and Tyler Huntley expected to miss the rest of the season with turf toe, coach Jesse Minter named Fagnano as the Ravens' starting quarterback for Week 9 on Tuesday. However, news broke Wednesday that Baltimore is finalizing a trade to acquire quarterback Jacoby Brissett, casting doubt on Fagnano's place in the pecking order. It looks like he'll ultimately take a back seat to Brissett starting in Week 10, but since the trade won't be finalized in time for Brissett to be available for the Ravens on Thursday, Fagnano still projects to start versus the Jaguars.

items.head: Named Week 9 starter
items.body: Ravens head coach Jesse Minter confirmed Tuesday that Fagnano (ankle) will start Thursday's game against the Jaguars, Jamison Hensley of ESPN.com reports.
