items.head: David Montgomery (Groin) is Out
items.body: Texans head coach DeMeco Ryans said Wednesday that Montgomery (groin) has made some progress but is still viewed as week-to-week and will remain out for Sunday's game against the Chargers, Jonathan M. Alexander of the Houston Chronicle reports.

items.head: Not seen at practice
items.body: Montgomery (groin) wasn't present for the portion of Wednesday's practice open to the media, Jonathan M. Alexander of the Houston Chronicle reports. Montgomery missed the Texans' two games before a Week 8 bye due to a groin issue, and his status remains up in the air as the team prepares for Sunday's contest at the Chargers. He hasn't practiced since sustaining the injury Oct. 11 at Tennessee, meaning he likely will need to mix into drills Thursday and/or Friday to have a chance to suit up this weekend.

items.head: Status uncertain for Week 9
items.body: Texans head coach DeMeco Ryans said Monday that he has "no significant update" on the status of Montgomery (groin) heading into a Week 9 matchup with the Chargers, Jonathan M. Alexander of the Houston Chronicle reports. Prior to the Texans' Week 8 bye, Montgomery missed two straight games due to a groin injury and wasn't able to practice in advance of either of those contests. Ryans didn't offer much of an indication that Montgomery's condition has dramatically improved following the bye, with the coach noting that the running back will be evaluated throughout the week before a decision is made on his status for Sunday's contest. If Montgomery ends up being sidelined for a third consecutive game, Woody Marks would be in store for another turn as Houston's lead back.

items.head: Brenen Thompson (Quadriceps) is Doubtful
items.body: doubtful

items.head: Set to start Sunday
items.body: Milton is set to be the Eagles' starting quarterback Sunday against the Giants, Mike Garafolo of NFL Network reports. Philadelphia signed Milton off the Cowboys' practice squad Oct. 16, and less than a month later, he's getting the call after the Tanner McKee experience so far has resulted in three consecutive losses. In five appearances (no starts) between New England and Dallas in his career, Milton has competed 37 of 53 passes for 424 yards, two touchdowns and two interceptions while rushing 15 times for 66 yards and one TD and losing both of his fumbles.

items.head: Won't play in Week 9
items.body: Head coach Mike Macdonald announced that Darnold won't play Sunday against the Cardinals due to a quadriceps injury, NFL reporter Andrew Siciliano reports. In addition to a quad issue that Darnold sustained late in Monday's loss to the Bears, Macdonald revealed that the quarterback suffered a rib injury early in that contest. The pair of health concerns may have played a part in Darnold's subpar performance, which included 188 yards, two touchdowns and one interception on 17-for-34 passing and two carries for 20 yards. With Darnold out for the first time since Week 2, backup QB Drew Lock will draw the Week 9 start under center for the Seahawks.

items.head: Middling numbers in Week 8 loss
items.body: Darnold completed 17 of 34 passes for 188 yards with two touchdowns and one interception while adding two rushes for 20 yards in the Seahawks' 34-17 loss to the Bears on Monday night. Darnold averaged just 5.5 yards per attempt and took three sacks from a Bears defense that made an impact addition in Jeffery Simmons on Thursday via trade with the Titans. Darnold's 50.0 percent completion rate was a season low for him in non-injury-shortened games, and the veteran signal-caller also threw an interception for the sixth consecutive contest. Darnold did toss multiple touchdowns for the first time since Week 4, connecting with Jaxon Smith-Njigba (43 yards) and Cooper Kupp (seven yards) for his pair of scoring strikes. Darnold will take an unsightly 10:9 TD:INT heading into a Week 9 home matchup against the Cardinals on Sunday.

items.head: No timetable for return
items.body: When asked Wednesday when Pierce (heel) might be able to return to practice, Colts head coach Shane Steichen noted that he "can't put a timetable on it right now," Kevin Bowen of 107.5 The Fan Indianapolis reports. Steichen said that Pierce, who has been on IR since Sept. 26, is currently rehabbing his injury, but the wideout's return is clearly not imminent. At 2-6, the Colts, who are already sellers ahead of the NFL trade deadline, have little incentive to rush Pierce back. Meanwhile, fellow WR Josh Downs has asked to be dealt, a situation that further clouds the team's pass-catching corps ahead of Week 9.

items.head: Alec Pierce (Heel) is Injured Reserve
items.body: When asked Wednesday when Pierce (heel) might be able to return to practice, Colts head coach Shane Steichen noted that he "can't put a timetable on it right now," Kevin Bowen of 107.5 The Fan Indianapolis reports.

items.head: Done for season with foot injury
items.body: McNichols, who suffered a foot injury Sunday against the Eagles that may require surgery, is out for the season, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports. McNichols was placed on injured reserve Tuesday, and what coach Dan Quinn described as a "serious mid-foot injury" will keep the running back sidelined for the rest of the 2026 campaign. With Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) slated to miss at least two more games, the Commanders' current healthy RBs are Rachaad White, Austin Ekeler and Robert Henry.

items.head: Heads to injured reserve
items.body: The Commanders placed McNichols (foot) on injured reserve Tuesday. McNichols' move to IR ensures that he'll miss at least the Commanders' next four games, but Tashan Reed of The Washington Post relays that the running back isn't expected to play again this season after sustaining what head coach Dan Quinn labeled as a "serious mid-foot injury" during Sunday's win over the Eagles. The 30-year-old is still seeking further medical opinions, so a formal timeline for McNichols' recovery hasn't yet been established. In response to McNichols' injury, Washington claimed Robert Henry off waivers from Seattle on Tuesday to bolster their depth at running back behind Rachaad White and Austin Ekeler.

items.head: May miss months
items.body: McNichols is getting additional opinions on the foot injury that he suffered Sunday against the Eagles, but there's an expectation that he'll miss multiple months, Tashan Reed of The Washington Post reports. McNichols limped to the locker room in the third quarter of Sunday's game in the third quarter and didn't return. Head coach Dan Quinn told Nicki Jhabvala of The Athletic on Monday that McNichols has a "mid-foot" injury that may be "serious," and Reed's new report backs up that sentiment. With Jacory Croskey-Merritt out at least three more games while on IR due to a groin issue, Rachaad White and Austin Ekeler are the healthy running backs on the Commanders' active roster.

items.head: Mid-foot injury is concerning
items.body: Commanders head coach Dan Quinn said Monday that McNichols has a "mid-foot" injury and is concerned that the running back is dealing with something "serious," Nicki Jhabvala of The Athletic reports. McNichols is scheduled to undergo further testing Tuesday before the Commanders provide an updated diagnosis, but the 30-year-old looks like he could be at risk of missing time, if not requiring a stint on injured reserve. With Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) already on IR and in line to miss at least two more games, the Commanders may need add backfield depth behind Rachaad White and Austin Ekeler in the coming days. In addition to the possibility of adding a free-agent running back, the Commanders also have Devin Neal and Craig Reynolds on their practice squad.

items.head: Questionable to return due to foot
items.body: McNichols (foot) is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Eagles. The Commanders clarified the nature of McNichols' injury shortly after he headed to the locker room while exhibiting a limp in the third quarter. Prior to getting hurt, McNichols had five carries for 21 yards and caught his only target for seven yards while working in a rotational role alongside Rachaad White and Austin Ekeler in the absence of Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin).

items.head: Injured against Eagles
items.body: McNichols headed back to the locker room in the second half of Sunday's game against the Eagles and was walking with a limp, Tashan Reed of The Washington Post reports. McNichols was checked for an injury in the blue tent before heading to the locker room. While the exact nature of his injury has yet to be clarified, the running back can be considered questionable to return after rushing five times for 21 yards and catching his lone target for seven yards prior to exiting. Rachaad White and Austin Ekeler are the two remaining healthy options in Washington's backfield rotation.

items.head: Another quiet performance Week 8
items.body: Higbee caught one of two targets for 14 yards against the Chargers in Sunday's 24-9 victory. Higbee logged a hearty 83 percent offensive snap share, most among Rams tight ends. However, he got little attention from quarterback Matthew Stafford, recording just two targets. Higbee had a nice run in Weeks 3-5, when he logged 18 catches for 212 yards across the three-game span. However, since then he's posted just seven receptions for 50 yards across his subsequent three contests. As such, it's hard to trust Higbee on a week-to-week basis right now even with the Rams down multiple pass catchers in Davante Adams (hamstring - IR), Terrance Ferguson (ankle - IR) and Colby Parkinson (ribs).

items.head: Dean Connors (Hand) is Injured Reserve
items.body: Connors (hand) was placed on IR on Tuesday, Blaine Grisak of SI.com reports.

items.head: Climbs up depth chart
items.body: Fehoko is listed as a starting receiver on the Cardinals' unofficial depth chart heading into Sunday's game at Seattle, Bo Brack of GoPHNX.com reports. Buried on the depth chart at receiver to begin the season, Fehoko mostly served as a special-teams contributor through the Cardinals' first seven games. However, with the Cardinals trading away Marvin Harrison before losing Jalen Brooks (wrist) and Kendrick Bourne (tibia) to season-ending injuries within the past two weeks, Fehoko suddenly finds himself in a position to contribute. After Bourne made an early exit in this past Sunday's 33-30 overtime victory over the Cowboys, Fehoko played double-digit snaps for the first time in 2026. He wasn't much of a factor in the Cardinals' comeback win, however, earning just one target (for a 17-yard reception) while taking the field for 40 of the team

items.head: James Conner (Foot) is Injured Reserve
items.body: Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur said Tuesday that Conner (foot) won't return from IR this week, Darren Urban of the team's official site reports.

items.head: Set for lead-back duties
items.body: Allgeier is slated to work as Arizona's No. 1 running back for at least the next four weeks after Jeremiyah Love (ankle) was placed on injured reserve Tuesday, Darren Urban of the team's official site reports. Allgeier previously led the Cardinals' backfield when Love was sidelined due to a different ankle injury Weeks 6 and 7, but Allgeier is now slated for a longer period in that role. Love was hurt late in the first quarter in his return to action Sunday against Dallas, and Allgeier ran wild after his departure, finishing with a career-high 147 yards and a touchdown on 11 carries along with 44 yards and another score on five receptions. In addition to Love getting hurt, Bam Knight suffered a concussion and is iffy to be able to suit up this Sunday against Seattle, so the backfield could belong to Allgeier, Evan Hull and a practice-squad signee (likely Jerome Ford). Though Allgeier found substan

items.head: Breaks out after RB injuries
items.body: Allgeier reeled off 147 yards and one touchdown on 11 carries and gathered in all five targets for 44 yards and one more TD during Sunday's 33-30 overtime win in Dallas. Fellow RBs Jeremiyah Love (ankle) and Bam Knight (concussion) left in the second and third quarters, respectively, and were unable to return, leaving Allgeier as the only healthy and available backfield option the rest of the way. Allgeier didn't really get going until QB Gardner Minshew took over for Jacoby Brissett late in the third quarter, as the running back recorded a 63-yard touchdown run, another 52-yard carry and a five-yard TD grab on the next two drives to account for most of his output. Considering Love has been dealing with ankle issues for most of the season and already has missed two games, and Knight is subject to the protocol for head injuries, Allgeier may be in line for a

items.head: Ready for Sunday
items.body: Allgeier (toe) doesn't have a designation for Sunday's contest at Dallas, Josh Weinfuss of ESPN.com reports. Allgeier kicked off Week 8 prep as a non-participant due to a toe injury, but he was able to log back-to-back limited sessions to end it, which was enough to get the all-clear for Sunday's matchup. He'll be welcoming back Jeremiyah Love (ankle) to the Cardinals backfield after a two-game absence, so the breakdown of reps between those two and potentially Bam Knight remains to be seen.

items.head: Scooped up by Saints
items.body: The Saints claimed Estime off waivers from the Browns on Tuesday. New Orleans released kicker Daniel Carlson to clear room on the 53-man roster for Estime, who began the season with the Saints before being cut on an injury settlement Sept. 22. After moving past a thigh injury, Estime caught on with the Browns and made his lone appearance for the team back in Week 6, when he carried nine times for 19 yards and a touchdown in a win over the Ravens. Upon rejoining the Saints, Estime will provide depth to a backfield that also includes Alvin Kamara, Kendre MIller and CJ Donaldson (shoulder).

items.head: Kendrick Bourne (Lower Leg) is Injured Reserve
items.body: Arizona placed Bourne (tibia) on injured reserve Tuesday, Darren Urban of the Cardinals' official site reports.

items.head: Out for season
items.body: Bourne suffered a fractured right tibia during Sunday's overtime win at Dallas that won't require surgery but will sideline him for three months, ending his 2026 season, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports. What was initially believed to be a right high-ankle sprain for Bourne has since been revealed to be much more serious after additional testing. He thus will finish with 26 catches (on 38 targets) for 263 yards and no touchdowns in eight regular-season appearances. With Marvin Harrison getting shipped to Houston on Oct. 11, Michael Wilson dealing with broken ribs and Jalen Brooks (wrist) out for the season, Reggie Virgil, Simi Fehoko and Devin Duvernay are the only healthy wide receivers on Arizona's active roster.

items.head: Expected to miss rest of season
items.body: Bourne (ankle) is expected to miss the remainder of the season, Jonathan Jones of The Athletic reports. Darren Urban of Cardinals' official site previously reported that head coach Mike LaFleur noted Monday that the ankle injury Bourne suffered Sunday against the Cowboys could be season-ending, and Jones' report further advances the notion that the wideout is slated to miss extended time. With Michael Wilson dealing with a rib issue, look for the Cardinals to add depth in short order to a WR corps that also includes Reggie Virgil, Simi Fehoko and Devin Duvernay.

items.head: Could face season-ending ankle injury
items.body: Coach Mike LaFleur noted Monday that the ankle injury Bourne suffered Sunday against the Cowboys could be season-ending,  Darren Urban of Cardschatter reports. Until further information is provided, it sounds like Bourne is on track to miss time, further taxing the health and depth of Arizona's WR corps, with Michael Wilson dealing with a rib issue. Reggie Virgil, Simi Fehoko and Devin Duvernay are next up in the pecking order behind Wilson and Bourne, but if Bourne indeed faces an extended absence, the Cardinals figure to seek additional personnel at the position.

items.head: Won't reenter Sunday's game
items.body: Bourne won't return to Sunday's contest at Dallas due to a right high-ankle sprain, Theo Mackie of The Arizona Republic reports. Bourne went the locker room late in the first half Sunday, and his eventual diagnosis means he'll miss not only the rest of Sunday's matchup, but likely multiple games beyond Week 8. With Bourne sidelined, Reggie Virgil, Simi Fehoko and Devin Duvernay will be the Cardinals' WR options not named Michael Wilson.

items.head: Heads to locker room Sunday
items.body: Bourne sustained an apparent right leg injury late in the second quarter of Sunday's game against the Cowboys and headed to the locker room, Josh Weinfuss of ESPN.com reports. Bourne went down with the injury on a non-contact play while he was running a route. The Cardinals should have an update available on Bourne's status following halftime. He finished the first half with a 29-yard reception on two targets.

items.head: Could land on IR
items.body: Ravens head coach Jesse Minter said Tuesday that Huntley (toe) could be a candidate for injured reserve, Sam Cohn of The Baltimore Sunreports. Following Sunday's 36-10 loss to the Bills, Minter confirmed that Lamar Jackson required thumb surgery and was ticketed for IR, and Huntley looks like he could join Jackson in being deactivated. Minter said that he expects to know by Wednesday whether Huntley will require an IR stint, as the Ravens are presumably still waiting on test results on the signal-caller's right toe injury. At the very least, Huntley is tracking toward sitting out Thursday's game against the Jaguars, as Minter announced Tuesday that undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano will serve as the Ravens' Week 9 starter.

items.head: Sidelined for practice Tuesday
items.body: Huntley (toe) wasn't spotted practicing Tuesday, Jamison Hensley of ESPN.com reports. Ravens head coach Jesse Minter already announced Monday that Huntley was "probably" not going to be ready to play in Thursday's game against the Jaguars, so the 28-year-old signal-caller is unlikely to practice at any point leading up to the contest. Joe Fagnano (ankle) was seen taking part in practice Tuesday as at least a limited participant and appears to be trending toward making his first NFL start Thursday, with either the newly signed Kedon Slovis or practice-squad member Austin Reed serving as his top backup. With Lamar Jackson (thumb) headed for injured reserve and set to miss at least the next four games, Huntley could be cleared to take over as the starting quarterback as soon as

items.head: May have turf-toe injury
items.body: Huntley sustained what could be a turf-toe injury during Sunday's 36-10 loss at Buffalo, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports. Huntley took over the offense after Lamar Jackson injured his right thumb on the Ravens' first offensive snap of the game. Huntley himself lasted into the third quarter until he was knocked from the contest with a toe issue. Head coach Jesse Minter relayed to Ryan Mink of the team's official site afterward that Jackson is slated for thumb surgery and will be placed on IR, while Huntley now may be dealing with a multi-week health concern of his own. Huntley will undergo an MRI on Monday to determine the official diagnosis and potential prognosis, but if he also joins Jackson on the pine, undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano (undisclosed) likely will be under center for Baltimore this Thursday against

items.head: Status uncertain due to toe injury
items.body: The status of Huntley (toe) is uncertain ahead of Thursday night's game against the Jaguars,  Tom Pelissero of Netflix reports Per Giana Han of TheBaltimoreBanner.com, Huntley was seen after Sunday's loss to the Bills with an evident limp. With franchise QB Lamar Jackson headed to IR with a thumb injury that could be season-ending, Huntley's status going forward gains plenty of import. For now, Joe Fagnano is the Ravens' healthiest signal-caller, but look for the team to add depth at the position in the coming days.

items.head: Ruled out for rest of Sunday's contest
items.body: Huntley (toe) has been ruled out for the rest of Sunday's game against the Bills. With Sunday starter Lamar Jackson also out for the remainder of the contest due to a right thumb injury, Joe Fagnano has been pressed into QB duties versus Buffalo. As a result of the pair of injuries at the position, Baltimore's signal-caller situation will need to be closely monitored ahead of Thursday night's game against the Jaguars.

items.head: Exit's Sunday's game
items.body: Huntley (toe) is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Bills. With Jackson (right thumb) having previously been ruled out for the remainder of the contest, Joe Fagnano - the Ravens' emergency No. 3 QB on Sunday -- has taken over for Huntley. Prior to hurting his toe, Huntley completed two of his four passing attempts for zero yards and was sacked once.

items.head: Reverting to backup role for Week 8
items.body: Huntley will be the backup quarterback against the Bills on Sunday after Lamar Jackson (ankle) was cleared to return from a three-game absence, Ryan Mink of the Ravens' official site reports. Jackson was a full participant in all three practices during Week 8 prep, which was enough for the two-time MVP to be cleared to return for Sunday's road tilt. Huntley started in each of the Ravens' last three games, during which he has completed 68.0 percent of his passes for 664 yards, four touchdowns and one interception while adding 14 carries for 60 yards and a score. Huntley will be on standby in case Jackson aggravates his ankle issue in Week 8.

items.head: Spotted doing rehab work Tuesday
items.body: Brooks (core) was seen working off to the side during the Panthers' unofficial practice Tuesday, Joe Person of The Athletic reports. The Panthers haven't yet opened Brooks' 21-day practice window, but that might happen soon after head coach Dave Canales said Monday that the young running back would "potentially" be designated for return from injured reserve this week. Brooks hasn't played since Week 2 after undergoing core-muscle surgery, so he'll likely need to turn in multiple full practices before the Panthers are comfortable clearing him for game action. Once he's activated from IR, Brooks will likely handle a supporting role out of the backfield behind starter Chubba Hubbard.

items.head: Could start practicing soon
items.body: Panthers head coach Dave Canales said Monday that Brooks (core) will "potentially" be designated for return from injured reserve this week, Joe Person of The Athletic reports. Canales noted that Brooks still has some checkpoints he needs to hit in his recovery process before getting the green light to practice, but the running back looks to have at least made progress on some level since undergoing core-muscle surgery Sept. 23. The running back has already spent more than four games on IR and will be eligible to be added back to the 53-man roster whenever the Panthers deem him healthy. Once activated, Brooks will likely have to settle for a change-of-pace role behind lead back Chubba Hubbard.

items.head: Bound for IR with high-ankle sprain
items.body: Love was diagnosed Tuesday with a right high-ankle sprain, which is expected to send him to injured reserve and keep him out for 4-to-5 weeks, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports. Love was available to play Week 8 after missing the Cardinals' previous two games due to a left ankle issue, but he ended up exiting Sunday's 33-30 overtime win over the Cowboys late in the first quarter after tweaking his opposite ankle. Though the No. 3 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft was cleared to play in advance of Week 1 after previously sustaining a right high-ankle sprain in the preseason, he won't be as fortunate this time around now that he's sprained the same ankle for the second time in less than three months. The projected 4-to-5-week recovery timeline gives Love a chance at returning to action when first eligible to return from IR on Dec. 6 against the Eagles, but at least f

items.head: Dealing with 'new' ankle injury
items.body: Head coach Mike LaFleur said Monday that Love suffered a "new" ankle injury during Sunday's overtime win at Dallas, and that he'll have an update on the running back later this week, Josh Weinfuss of ESPN.com reports. Prior to having his right ankle rolled up on while getting tackled Sunday, Love was dealing with a left ankle issue, so this is a bit of a non-update from LaFleur. Having said that, LaFleur's last comment indicates that he may touch on the nature of Love's injury and also its prognosis in the near future. Fellow RB Bam Knight has entered the concussion protocol in the wake of Week 8 action, leaving Tyler Allgeier as the unquestioned healthy lead back for the Cardinals at the moment.

items.head: Not returning to Sunday's contest
items.body: Love (ankle) was ruled out for Sunday's game against the Cowboys to begin the second half, Alex Weiner of ArizonaSports.com reports. Love had sat out the Cardinals' prior two contests due to a left ankle injury, but he appeared to tweak the opposite ankle on a carry late in the first quarter of Sunday's game. After a brief visit to the medical tent on the Arizona sideline, Love retreated to the locker room, where he remained to begin the third quarter before the Cardinals ruled him out. Prior to his departure, Love carried nine times for 23 yards and didn't draw any targets. His status will warrant monitoring leading up to the Cardinals' Week 9 game against the Seahawks on Nov. 8.

items.head: Officially has ankle injury
items.body: Love (ankle) is questionable to return to Sunday's game at Dallas, Theo Mackie of The Arizona Republic reports. Love missed the previous two contests due to a left ankle injury, but after having his right ankle rolled up on in the second quarter Sunday, he visited the medical tent and then the locker room before the Cardinals clarified the nature of his injury. For as long as Love is off the field, Tyler Allgeier and Bam Knight will man Arizona's backfield.

items.head: Leaves for locker room Sunday
items.body: Love headed into the locker room during the second quarter of Sunday's game against the Cowboys to be further evaluated for an apparent lower-body injury, Josh Weinfuss of ESPN.com reports. Love had been sidelined for the Cardinals' previous two games due to a left ankle injury, but he appeared to check out of Sunday's contest after taking a hit to his right ankle/leg in the final minute of the first quarter. The Cardinals will examine him more thoroughly in the locker room before providing an update on the nature of his injury as well as his status for the remainder of the contest. Love carried nine times for 23 yards prior to departing.

items.head: Goes to sideline Sunday
items.body: Love (undisclosed) went to the sideline during Sunday's contest in Dallas, Darren Urban of the Cardinals' official site reports. Love appeared to get his right ankle rolled up on in the second quarter and remained on the turf for a spell before jogging to the sideline and going into the medical tent. He's been dealing with a left ankle injury that sidelined him the last two games, so this appears to be a new health concern.

items.head: Ready to return in Week 8
items.body: Love (ankle) doesn't have a designation for Sunday's game at Dallas, Josh Weinfuss of ESPN.com reports. Head coach Mike LaFleur told Darren Urban of the Cardinals' official site Friday that Love was expected to play in Week 8, and the running back's lack of designation confirms as much. After opening the week with back-to-back limited listings, Love capped it with a full session Friday, indicating that he's ready for close to a normal workload Sunday after a two-game absence. Speaking of the time off, Love relayed to Urban that "two weeks for anybody will get people feeling how they want to feel." As a result, Love will rejoin a backfield that previously was a near-even split between Tyler Allgeier (toe) and Bam Knight the last two weeks.

items.head: In line to play Sunday
items.body: Coach Mike LaFleur said Friday that Love (ankle) is expected to play in Sunday's game against the Cowboys, Darren Urban of the Cardinals' official site reports. In his return to drills this week following a two-game absence, Love has managed a pair of limited practices as he seeks to put an ankle injury behind him. It's unclear if Love will enter the weekend with a designation for Sunday's game at Dallas, something that'll be revealed on Friday's practice report. As for the rest of Arizona's backfield, Tyler Allgeier is tending to a toe issue, leaving just Bam Knight as a healthy option at the position.

items.head: Relegated to special teams Monday
items.body: Wilson played just seven snaps -- all on special teams -- in Monday's 34-17 loss to the Bears. After logging double-digit carries in six of the Seahawks' previous seven games while scoring four touchdowns and averaging 66.4 scrimmage yards during that span, Wilson fell out of the game plan entirely in Week 8. With Zach Charbonnet (knee) getting cleared to make his 2026 debut, Jadarian Price (chest) returning from injured reserve and George Holani still on hand as an option on passing downs, the Seahawks had no reps available out of the backfield for Wilson. Unless Charbonnet or Price succumbs to another injury, Wilson's playing time on offense will likely remain scarce moving forward.

items.head: More competition for work
items.body: Wilson is welcoming back Zach Charbonnet (knee) and Jadarian Price (chest) to the Seahawks backfield for Monday's game against the Bears, John Boyle of the team's official site reports. Seattle cleared Charbonnet to make his season debut on its final Week 8 injury report before the team activated Price from injured reserve Monday, which means the latter is available for his first game action since Week 3. Wilson operated as the Seahawks' lead runner the last four contests, racking up 85 touches for 359 yards from scrimmage and four total TDs. He'll certainly cede some of those reps to the combination of Charbonnet and Price, but the possibility exists that he ends up taking on the most work among the trio if the team eases one or both back in.

items.head: Pair of catches in Week 8 loss
items.body: Barner brought in two of five targets for 23 yards in the Seahawks' 34-17 loss to the Bears on Monday night. Barner was third in receiving yards and targets, although the tight end still finished below 30 receiving yards for the sixth time this season. Barner remained in a minor role despite the fact the Seahawks were down Rashid Shaheed (knee), and with 21 receptions for 203 yards and zero touchdowns, the third-year pro remains behind the pace of his career-best 52-519-6 line from last season. Barner will look to capitalize on a favorable matchup against the Cardinals defense in a Week 9 home matchup on Sunday.

items.head: Nine touches in season debut
items.body: Charbonnet (knee) rushed six times for 23 yards and brought in three of four targets for six yards in the Seahawks' 34-17 loss to the Bears on Monday night. Charbonnet took the first carry of the night for Seattle, gaining an encouraging five yards on his first tote since tearing his left ACL in a divisional-round win over the 49ers in January. He also subsequently rattled off a 13-yard gain in the third quarter, but he was limited on his other touches and ultimately had four fewer rush attempts than Jadarian Price. Charbonnet's snap share and touches should gradually increase, and a Week 9 home matchup against the Cardinals could serve as a good platform for his workload to see a nice bump.

items.head: Works with starters in warmups
items.body: Charbonnet was "the first running back getting handoffs" during warmups before Monday's game against the Bears, Gregg Bell of The Tacoma News Tribune reports. Charbonnet is set to see his first action of the season Monday night, and with him first in line during warmups it appears he will jump right into Seattle's starting lineup. While Charbonnet will likely be the first man up in the backfield, he is coming off knee surgery and will be one of four Seahawks running backs available -- Jadarian Price, Emanuel Wilson and George Holani being the others -- so it's unclear exactly what type of workload he will handle in his season debut.

items.head: Will play Monday
items.body: Charbonnet (knee) does not carry an injury designation into Monday's game against the Bears, John Boyle of the Seahawks' official site reports. Charbonnet has been officially cleared to make his 2026 regular-season debut, marking the end to his rehab from a torn ACL in his left knee that he sustained in mid-January during the Seahawks' playoff run. The Seahawks' backfield will be whole for the first time this season, seeing as both Charbonnet and Jadarian Price (chest) have been cleared to play Monday, with Emanuel Wilson and George Holani providing depth.

items.head: Practices in limited capacity
items.body: Charbonnet (knee) was a limited participant in Friday's practice, John Boyle of the Seahawks' official site reports. Charbonnet opened Week 8 prep with a full practice Wednesday, which marked his fourth consecutive such listing on Seahawks injury reports. Having said that, his downgrade to limited could signify a setback of sorts as the running back seeks his first game action since Jan. 17, when he suffered a torn ACL in his left knee. Meanwhile, ellow RB Jadarian Price (chest), who was designated for return from injured reserve this week, went from limited Thursday to full Friday. In the end, Saturday's practice report will reveal both players odds to suit up Monday against the Bears.

items.head: Scores TD on only Week 8 reception
items.body: Kupp caught one of three targets for a seven-yard touchdown Monday in a loss to the Bears. Kupp had another low target share, but he at least made the most of his only catch by hauling in a seven-yard TD early in the fourth quarter. That score probably isn't going to be enough to inspire confidence in him in fantasy, though, given that the veteran wideout has drawn three or fewer targets in six of his eight games this season. Kupp's seven receiving yards Monday also were a season-low mark, and there simply doesn't seem to be much room for any wideout aside from Jaxon Smith-Njigba to regularly find success in Seattle's offense given Smith-Njigba's massive target share. With that said, Kupp at least will have a favorable matchup in Week 9, as he'll face an Arizona defense that has s

items.head: Gains 37 total yards in return
items.body: Price rushed 10 times for 29 yards and brought in two of four targets for eight yards in the Seahawks' 34-17 loss to the Bears on Monday night. Making his return from a four-game stay on injured reserve due to a chest injury, Price ended up leading the Seahawks' ground attack in carries and rushing yards. Price's return coincided with the season debut of Zach Charbonnet (knee), who logged six carries in his own right in a game whose script eventually turned unfriendly to the running game. Monday may have served as a preview of what might be expected in terms of the division of labor between the two players, but more information will be gleaned during a Week 9 home matchup against the Cardinals on Sunday that should afford both backs more opportunities.

items.head: Activated for Monday night game
items.body: The Seahawks reinstated Price (chest) from injured reserve ahead of Monday's game against the Bears, John Boyle of the team's official site reports. As Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reported earlier Monday, Price will be back in action for Seattle after a minimum-length four-game stint on IR. Price, who initially sustained a chest injury in Week 2 before being deactivated after experiencing an aggravation, carried 28 times for 119 yards and added four receptions for 21 yards on seven targets through Seattle's first three games. Though he closed Week 8 prep with a pair of full practices, Price may have to settle for a more muted role as part of a backfield committee in his return to action. Zach Charbonnet (knee) has been cleared to make his 2026 debut Monday, and Emanuel Wilson could also factor into the mix after rushing for a season-high

items.head: No designation for Week 8
items.body: Price (chest) doesn't have a designation for Monday's game against the Bears, but he remains on injured reserve, John Boyle of the Seahawks' official site reports. The Seahawks designated Price for return from IR on Thursday, and he proceeded to be limited that day and full Friday. Now that he's been given clearance for his first game action since Week 3 due to a chest injury, the team still needs to activate him from IR by Monday afternoon in order for him to be available in Week 8. Fellow RB Zach Charbonnet (knee) also doesn't have a designation this week, so Seattle's backfield suddenly is crowded, with Emanuel Wilson and George Holani also in the mix.

items.head: Practices fully Friday
items.body: Price (chest) was a full participant in Friday's practice, John Boyle of the Seahawks' official site reports. Since the Seahawks designated Price for return from injured reserve Thursday, he logged a limited session in his first chance to do so, followed by Friday's uncapped practice. How he's listed on Saturday's injury report will determine if he has a chance to return in Week 8 against the Bears, and if he's anything but 'Out' he'll need to be activated from IR by Monday afternoon and then be deemed active that evening. Meanwhile, fellow RB Zach Charbonnet (knee) went from full Thursday to limited Friday, seemingly indicating he may be trending in the wrong direction to make his season sebut.

items.head: Racks up 53 total yards on MNF
items.body: Raymond finished Monday's 34-17 win against Seattle with two catches for 14 yards on three targets along with one rush for 39 yards. Raymond's most memorable contribution was a 39-yard dash on a third-down play early in the fourth quarter to take the ball down to Seattle's five-yard line and set up a D'Andre Swift touchdown. Though he didn't put up massive numbers, Raymond's 53 total yards were his most since Week 3 and represented more yardage than he had recorded over his previous four games combined. Raymond remains a shaky fantasy play given his recent numbers, and a Week 9 matchup against a Tampa Bay defense that has been pretty stingy on wideouts doesn't improve his outlook.

items.head: Team-high yardage total in win
items.body: Odunze brought in four of six targets for 87 yards in the Bears' 34-17 win over the Seahawks on Monday night. Odunze led the Bears in receiving yards on the night while finishing second in receptions and targets. The third-year wideout's catch and yardage totals both qualified as his second highest of the season, and Odunze now has 156 receiving yards over the last pair of contests for his most productive two-game stretch this season. Odunze is averaging a career-best 16.7 yards per catch and already has a career-high 14 receptions of 20-plus yards heading into a Week 9 home matchup against the Buccaneers on Sunday night.

items.head: Stays busy in Week 8 win
items.body: Burden secured seven of nine targets for 56 yards and a touchdown in the Bears' 34-17 win over the Seahawks on Monday night. Burden tied Colston Loveland for the team lead in both receptions and targets, and he was on the receiving end of Caleb Williams' one touchdown pass of the night. The second-year wideout's scoring grab came from one yard out in the first quarter and was his third of the season, and Burden now has a 19-281-2 line on 21 targets over the last three games heading into a Week 9 home matchup against the Buccaneers on Sunday night.

items.head: Co-team-high catch total in win
items.body: Loveland secured seven of nine targets for 65 yards and lost a fumble in the Bears' 34-17 win over the Seahawks on Monday night. Loveland continued his upward trajectory by tying Luther Burden for the team lead in catches and targets, and he finished second in receiving yards to Rome Odunze. The second-year tight end's fourth-quarter fumble was costly for the moment, however, as Loveland lost the ball at the Bears' 21-yard line following an eight-yard reception, and the turnover ultimately led to the Seahawks' final touchdown of the contest. Nevertheless, Loveland now has at least six receptions in four of the last five games, including three straight, and he's drawn 21 targets over the last pair of contests alone heading into a Week 9 home matchup against the Buccaneers on Sunday night.

items.head: Cleared for Monday Night Football
items.body: Loveland (neck) does not carry an injury designation into Monday's game against the Seahawks. Loveland popped up on Friday's injury report as a limited practice participant due to a neck injury. However, the second-year tight end was able to practice without restriction Saturday and is good to go for Monday's game. His availability for Week 8 and beyond is particularly important given that Cole Kmet (knee, IR) is out for the rest of the 2026 season. Loveland has caught 25 passes (on 37 targets) for 241 yards and two touchdowns over his last five outings.

items.head: Limited Friday by neck issue
items.body: Loveland was limited at Friday's practice due to a neck injury, Kevin Fishbain of The Athletic reports. Loveland is making a midweek appearance on the Bears' Week 8 injury report, which may be cause for concern ahead of Monday's game at Seattle. In the end, though, Saturday's practice report will determine if he has a designation for that matchup.

items.head: Three-TD night in win
items.body: Swift rushed 27 times for 69 yards and three touchdowns and brought in two of three targets for 10 yards in the Bears' 34-17 win over the Seahawks on Monday night. Swift put in a full night's work while repeatedly butting heads with the Seahawks' elite run defense, as his longest run went for only seven yards, and he averaged 2.6 yards per carry overall. He sealed the win for Chicago with his third touchdown of the game, a five-yard run with 4:41 remaining. That score was preceded by one- and five-yard TDs earlier in the second half, and Swift's carry total was a season high. The veteran running back is up to a career-high 10 rushing touchdowns heading into a Week 9 home matchup against the Buccaneers on Sunday night.

items.head: Another 100-yard effort in loss
items.body: Smith-Njigba brought in six of 11 targets for 118 yards and a touchdown in the Seahawks' 34-17 loss to the Bears on Monday night. Smith-Njigba was in his usual position of leading the Seahawks across the board in receptions, receiving yards and targets, and he crossed the 100-yard mark for the seventh time in eight games this season with a pair of catches on Seattle's final drive of the night. His target total also was his sixth double-digit tally of the campaign, and the absence of Rashid Shaheed (knee) helped reinforce JSN's downfield role even further. Smith-Njigba now will head into a Week 9 home matchup against the Cardinals on Sunday just 15 yards short of his third consecutive 1,000-yard campaign and only a touchdown shy of tying the career-high 10 he recorded over 17 regular-season games last season.

items.head: No grabs in Week 8 win
items.body: Engram failed to catch any of his three targets in Sunday's 28-24 win over the Chiefs. Bo Nix targeted 10 different pass catchers on 32 total pass attempts, and it was rookie RB Jonah Coleman who led the team in receiving with a 4-63-0 line on five targets. Engram has just three catches for 15 yards over his last three games and isn't a recommended fantasy bet ahead of Sunday's date with the Panthers.

items.head: Catches 22-yard pass in loss
items.body: Bateman caught one of three targets for 22 yards in Sunday's 36-10 loss to the Bills. Bateman actually led the Ravens in receiving yards on a day in which three quarterbacks attempted passes for Baltimore. Since posting a 7-88-1 receiving line in Week 2 against the Saints, Bateman has totaled 12 grabs for 200 yards and no scores over his last six games. He has minimal fantasy appeal while Zay Flowers is healthy.

items.head: One catch against Rams
items.body: Kolar caught one of four targets for 20 yards in Sunday's 24-9 loss to the Rams. The tight end's four targets tied for third on the team, as he ran 17 routes on Justin Herbert's 37 dropbacks against Los Angeles. More of a blocker than receiver, Kolar has been forced to catch more passes out of necessity at times this season. He has 10 grabs for 98 yards on 17 targets. The catches and targets are both career highs in his fifth season.

items.head: Totals 19 yards against Tennessee
items.body: Perine rushed four times for 10 yards and caught his lone target for nine yards in Sunday's 43-36 overtime win over the Titans. The Bengals were chasing the Titans on the scoreboard much of the afternoon, and Chase Brown and Perine combined for just 16 carries, as Joe Burrow fired off 48 pass attempts. Perine is a touchdown-or-bust desperation RB3 in fantasy whose main value comes in the form of being Brown's backup. Cincinnati has been linked to a potential trade for a running back ahead of next week's deadline.

items.head: Doesn't see field in Week 8
items.body: Mendoza didn't play in Sunday's 38-33 win over the Jets. With Kirk Cousins helping orchestrate a second-half comeback, Mendoza stayed glued to the sideline for the third straight contest after playing 10 offensive snaps in Week 5 against New England. The Raiders are 4-4 with Cousins playing reasonably well to keep the team in the postseason mix. Mendoza figures to get his shot if/when the Raiders are eliminated from postseason contention.

items.head: One grab in loss to Las Vegas
items.body: Sadiq caught one of two targets for 22 yards in Sunday's 38-33 loss to the Raiders. The rookie tight end played 31 of 64 offensive snaps against Las Vegas and ran just 15 routes on Geno Smith's 35 dropbacks. Sadiq continues to play behind Mason Taylor, who recorded three grabs for 19 yards on five targets across 19 routes. The Jets are using four tight ends on game days, and this offense isn't able to support more than a couple pass catchers for fantasy each week. Outside of his 7-105-1 receiving performance in Week 3 against the Lions, Sadiq has a total of 10 catches for 79 yards across his seven other contests.

items.head: No catches again in Week 8 win
items.body: Otton wasn't targeted in Sunday's 16-0 win over the Falcons. Playing in rain-soaked conditions, the Bucs attempted just three passes all afternoon, as Baker Mayfield failed to complete any of the three. Otton now has posted back-to-back zero-catch games and has minimal fantasy appeal outside of the deepest of TE-premium formats. He has 19 grabs for 186 yards and no touchdowns on 30 targets through eight games.

items.head: Totals 23 yards in loss to Rams
items.body: Mitchell rushed four times for six yards and caught all three of his targets for 17 yards in Sunday's 24-9 loss to the Rams. Handpicked by first-year OC Mike McDaniel as a free-agent signing in the offseason, Mitchell has been a total non-factor for much of the first half of the season. With a career 5.7 yards per carry average, Mitchell is averaging just 3.7 yards per rush this season. Involved in a three-way backfield committee with Omarion Hampton and Kimani Vidal, Mitchell is waiver-wire fodder in normal-sized 12-team fantasy leagues.

items.head: Tallies 30 rushing yards in win
items.body: Davis rushed six times for 30 yards in Sunday's 36-10 win over the Ravens. With the Bills throttling the Ravens and James Cook suffering a neck injury late in the game, Davis got some added run in the fourth quarter. If Cook misses any time, Davis would be the likely early-down replacement, with Ty Johnson sticking to his role on passing downs and four- and two-minute situations.

items.head: Quiet Sunday despite extended opportunity
items.body: Raridon had one reception for five yards on four targets in New England's 24-19 win over the Dolphins on Sunday. Raridon's lone reception went for five yards early in the first quarter. He didn't record another catch for the remainder of the contest despite logging a hefty 93 percent offensive snap share, largely due to No .1 tight end Hunter Henry departing in the first half due to a foot injury. Should Henry remain sidelined in Week 9, Raridon will have another big opportunity to produce in a home tilt against Green Bay.

items.head: Leads team in rushing in loss
items.body: Vidal rushed eight times for 23 yards and caught both of his targets for seven yards in Sunday's 24-9 loss to the Rams. The Chargers continue to use a fantasy-unfriendly three-man backfield, giving all three of Vidal, Omarion Hampton and Keaton Mitchell meaningful touches and snaps. In a broken Los Angeles offense and crowded group of RBs, Vidal has minimal fantasy appeal outside of deeper formats.

items.head: Three grabs in Week 8 defeat
items.body: Ayomanor caught three of five targets for 34 yards in Sunday's 43-36 overtime loss to the Bengals. Even with Carnell Tate (shoulder) inactive against Cincinnati, Ayomanor's role didn't grow much, as Wan'Dale Robinson, Gunnar Helm and Chimere Dike combined to see 22 of the team's 39 targets. Through eight games this season, Ayomanor has 13 grabs for 211 yards and a touchdown on 26 targets.

items.head: Expanded role for Week 8 sans Tate
items.body: Carnell Tate (shoulder) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Bengals, leaving Ayomanor and Wan'Dale Robinson as the top wide receivers in the passing game, Jim Wyatt of the Titans' official site reports. Tate has been the bright spot in what otherwise has been a dreadful Titans passing game this season, so the absence of the rookie fourth overall pick means Ayomanor, Robinson and running back Tony Pollard are all in line for more targets from second-year quarterback Cam Ward. Ayomanor saw a season-high seven targets in Week 7 against the Browns, but he reached that mark five times during his rookie year in 2025 and is capable of handling a larger role, even if Calvin Ridley (shoulder) is available. Through seven regular-season games, Ayomanor has 10 catches (on 21 targets) for 177 yards and a touchdown.

items.head: Leads Colts in rushing yards in season debut
items.body: Giddens racked up 43 yards on six carries in Indianapolis' Week 8 loss to Jacksonville on Sunday. Giddens entered Sunday having not logged a snap this season, but he got an opportunity in the blowout loss and made the most of it, ripping off a pair of 12-yard runs on the way to a team-leading 43 rushing yards. However, it must be noted that he didn't enter until the game was far out of reach in the fourth quarter, so all of his production came in garbage time. Still, it was a meaningful performance by Giddens in the context of Indianapolis fielding trade offers for star RB Jonathan Taylor amidst a lost season. Should Taylor indeed be dealt, Giddens would immediately take on a more prominent role in the Colts backfield along with seventh-round rookie Seth McGowan.

items.head: Breaks one long run Week 8
items.body: McGowan rushed five times for 29 yards and returned four kickoffs for 103 yards Sunday in a loss to the Jaguars. McGowan's best run was a 16-yarder up the middle midway through the third quarter to take the ball to Jacksonville's three-yard line. That set up Indianapolis' only touchdown in the blowout loss. McGowan logged a modest 15 offensive snaps to starter Jonathan Taylor's 38, but the former outgained Taylor on the ground, 29-23. Meanwhile, DJ Giddens paced the Colts with 43 rushing yards on six totes. The big story, of course, is that the Colts are entertaining trade offers on Taylor, and if the star RB is ultimately dealt, McGowan and Giddens both figure to take on significantly larger roles, though it's unclear which of the two would become the starter. With that in mind, it's worth noting that

items.head: Musters two catches in Week 8
items.body: Okonkwo tallied two catches (on four targets) for 32 yards during Sunday's 27-10 win versus the Eagles. Okonkwo logged a typical 77 percent snap share in Week 8, but aside from a stellar 21-yard catch in the fourth quarter, he didn't contribute much to the Commanders offense. Overall, he's mustered just a 17-182-0 line on 24 targets in his five appearances this season, but 15 of his catches have occurred in the four full contests for Jayden Daniels in 2026, so the tight end has exhibited a rapport with the team's primary signal-caller. Okonkwo will aim for a bounceback this coming Sunday against the Rams.

items.head: Jacob Saylors (Neck) is Questionable
items.body: Saylors (neck) is not expected to practice Wednesday, Nolan Bianchi of The Detroit News reports.

items.head: Held without catch in Week 8
items.body: Jeudy did not catch his lone target Sunday in Cleveland's 27-6 loss to Pittsburgh. Quarterback Deshaun Watson had a relatively productive day with 324 passing yards (albeit without a score), but Jeudy was on the receiving end of only one of his passes. The veteran wideout logged his usual amount of playing time, notching a 60 percent offensive snap share to finish third among Cleveland wide receivers. It was the third time this season Jeudy has finished without a catch, but the other two instances were in Weeks 3 and 4, and he had been more involved of late, averaging 3.5 catches and 36.3 receiving yards over his previous four games. With that in mind, he could get back on track in Week 9 against a New Orleans defense that has been middle-of-the-pack against wideouts this

items.head: Held catchless by Jets
items.body: Tucker did not catch his only target Sunday in the Raiders' 38-33 Week 8 win over the Jets. Despite quarterback Kirk Cousins throwing for 247 yards, Tucker had only one ball thrown his way. In fact, only one Raiders wideout -- Jalen Nailor -- had a reception, as Cousins targeted tight ends on 16 of his 26 passes. Tucker had caught either four or five passes in each of his prior six games and collected at least 97 receiving yards in three of those contests, though he finished below 45 yards in the other three. It's notable that he logged a season-low 52 percent offensive snap share against the Jets, but he should be in for better days ahead, beginning with a Week 9 matchup in San Francisco.

items.head: Makes one catch in Week 8
items.body: Waller corralled one of two targets for 11 yards during last Thursday's 27-19 loss at Green Bay. Waller has been hit or miss from a fantasy perspective this season, with two touchdown grabs in Week 2 in Atlanta and a 50-yard TD catch in Week 7 against the Buccaneers serving as the notable performances. Otherwise, he has one 50-yard effort in his five other appearances, sitting on a 15-209-3 line on 25 targets on the season. Waller next takes aim at the tough Broncos defense this coming Sunday.

items.head: Moves up to second on depth chart
items.body: Head coach Mike LaFleur said that Beck will serve as the Cardinals' No. 2 quarterback behind starter Gardner Minshew in Sunday's game against the Seahawks, Darren Urban of the team's official site reports. Beck had been a healthy inactive through each of the Cardinals' first eight games of the season as the emergency No. 3 quarterback, but he'll get the chance to dress for the first time in Week 9 after Arizona removed the struggling Jacoby Brissett from the starting role and dropped him down two spots on the depth chart. Like Brissett, the 30-year-old Minshew is a journeyman who isn't viewed as the team's long-term solution under center, so it wouldn't be surprising if Beck eventually received a look as the starter before the end of the season if Arizona eventually fades from playoff contention. A rookie third-round pick out of Miami, Beck completed 15 of 19 pass attempts for 188 yards and a

items.head: Progressing in recovery
items.body: Stribling (ankle) was spotted Monday walking without crutches or a brace on his lower leg, Matt Barrows of The Athletic reports. Stribling, who garnered his share of preseason fantasy buzz, was injured in the 49ers' Week 1 win over the Rams, but it appears as though the wideout is making solid progress in his recovery. A firm timetable for the 2026 second-rounder's return to practice hasn't been outlined yet, but David Lombardi of SFStandard.com previously noted that Stribling (ankle) remains on track to return at some point in December, a notion supported by Barrows' report.

items.head: De'Zhaun Stribling (Ankle) is Injured Reserve
items.body: Stribling (ankle) was spotted Monday walking without crutches or a brace on his lower leg, Matt Barrows of The Athletic reports.

items.head: Taking over as starting quarterback
items.body: Head coach Mike LaFleur announced that Minshew will step in as the Cardinals' new starting quarterback beginning with Sunday's game at Seattle, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports. Unsurprisingly, the Cardinals have opted to appoint Minshew to the top spot on the depth chart after he came on in relief of a struggling Jacoby Brissett and led a stirring comeback in Sunday's 33-30 overtime win over the Cowboys. In what was his first appearance of the season, Minshew completed 17 of 23 pass attempts for 188 yards and three touchdowns in just under two quarters' worth of action before Chad Ryland sealed the victory with a walk-off 42-yard field goal. Though his performance in future games will ultimately dictate how long he sticks around as the Cardinals' starter, Minshew is far from a lock to hold down the job for the balance of the season. If the 3-5 Cardinals eventually

items.head: Leads Cards to comeback win
items.body: Minshew completed 17 of 23 passes for 188 yards, three touchdowns and no interceptions after he replaced starting QB Jacoby Brissett late in the third quarter of Sunday's 33-30 overtime win in Dallas. When Minshew took over the Cardinals offense with 1:35 remaining in the third quarter, the team was trailing 17-3, and he proceeded to direct four consecutive TD drives, which ended (in order) with a 63-yard run via RB Tyler Allgeier, a five-yard catch from Allgeier, a 14-yard connection with TE Trey McBride and a 13-yard reception from WR Michael Wilson to force overtime. All three players were the top remaining options at their positions at the time, and Minshew ended up out-producing Brissett by 69 passing yards in roughly two fewer quarters of play. Afterward, head coach Mike LaFleur told Darren Urban of the team's official site that he won't commit to a starting QB for next Sunday's gam

items.head: Expected to remain with team
items.body: Head coach Matt LaFleur said Monday that the Packers are aware of the prior physical abuse allegations involving Jacobs that recently surfaced and "anticipate him being a member" of the team moving forward, Ryan Wood of USA Today reports. Before making his season debut Week 7, Jacobs missed the Packers' first six games after he was placed on the commissioner's exempt list after he was officially charged Aug. 27 with two misdemeanors stemming from his May arrest for a domestic incident. The legal process related to that incident has since played out, but Jacobs' status with the team had been called into question after the NFL announced Saturday that it was reviewing additional allegations of physical and verbal abuse from three different women in incidents dating back to April 2021 that were released following a public records request. Unless the NFL elects to place him back on the exempt list while it reviews the incidents in

items.head: Additional allegations emerge
items.body: "Newly released records," according to NBC 26, "show additional women contacted the Hobart/Lawrence Police Department to report alleged physical incidents involving Jacobs." Per the initial report, "The accounts surfaced during the department's investigation into a May 23 incident at Jacobs' home," and according to the Associated Press "were included in evidence regarding Jacobs' battery case," which he ultimately pleaded no contest to. The follow-up report notes that the NFL will "review these allegations as part of its investigation, which has remained open."

items.head: Sticking as starting quarterback
items.body: Head coach Shane Steichen said that Jones will remain the Colts' starting quarterback heading into Sunday's game against the Cowboys, Mike Chappell of Fox 59 News Indianapolis reports. After a 42-7 loss to the Jaguars on Sunday during which Jones was benched in favor of Anthony Richardson in the fourth quarter, Steichen suggested that he would evaluate every position, including quarterback. While some changes could still be afoot for the 2-6 Colts, Steichen will apparently stand pat at center with Jones, at least for one more week. After a promising first season in Indianapolis was cut short by a torn Achilles, Jones has been a major disappointment since reaching a two-year, $88 million extension with the Colts in March. Through eight games, Jones ranks 29th among 30 qualified quarterbacks in QBR (39.6) and is tied with the Chargers' Justin Herbert for the NFL lead with 12

items.head: May lose starting job
items.body: Head coach Shane Steichen said after Sunday's 42-7 loss at Jacksonville that he'll evaluate "everything, including whether" Jones remains the Colts' starting quarterback, James Boyd of The Athletic reports. Jones completed 19 of 28 passes for 144 yards, one touchdown (to WR Josh Downs) and two interceptions while rushing four times for seven yards in Week 8. He also yielded the Colts' final three drives to backup QB Anthony Richardson, who didn't fare much better (2-for-2 passing for eight yards, two rushes for four yards). Sunday's performance marked Jones' fourth (in eight appearances) in which he didn't reach 200 yards passing, and overall he's sitting on a 5:9 TD:INT on the campaign. Indianapolis is in the midst of a fire sale of its active roster, and handing the keys to the offense to Richardson to see how he looks in the second half may be in the cards.

items.head: Xavier Legette (Knee) is Injured Reserve
items.body: Panthers head coach Dave Canales said Monday that Legette (knee) will "potentially" be designated for return from injured reserve this week, Joe Person of The Athletic reports.

items.head: Michael Pittman Jr. (Foot) is Injured Reserve
items.body: Pittman (foot) said Monday that he resumed running last week as part of a program to return, but the wideout acknowledged that he's without a clear timeline to be activated from injured reserve, Ray Fittipaldo of the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette reports.

items.head: Five catches in blowout win
items.body: Bernard caught all five of his targets for 30 yards during Sunday's 27-6 win against Cleveland. Bernard led the team in catches, reeling in multiple passes for the fifth straight week and sixth time overall this year. The wide receiver has built a strong rapport with starting quarterback Aaron Rodgers, but it's unclear what Bernard's workload will look like after the Steelers have a chance to regroup and potentially acquire another pass catcher during the team's bye week in Week 9.

items.head: Four grabs in loss to Rams
items.body: Johnston caught all four of his targets for 37 yards in Sunday's 24-9 loss to the Rams. Johnston's four grabs marked a new personal single-game high through six games this season. One of the least efficient wideouts in the league, Johnston entered Sunday with just eight grabs for 165 yards on 22 targets. He hasn't been playable in fantasy football for weeks and will square off with a stingy Houston secondary in Week 9.

items.head: Bolts getting reinforcements for Week 8
items.body: Johnston's role in the passing game will shrink slightly in Week 8 against the Rams given that both Ladd McConkey (concussion) and Tre' Harris (hamstring) have been cleared to play, Eric Smith of the Chargers' official site reports. Both Johnston and McConkey were sidelined for Week 5, but the latter entered the league's concussion protocol during the Chargers' Week 6 loss to the Chiefs. Johnston logged 17 targets through his first three games of the regular season, although he's seen only five passes from Justin Herbert over his last two outings, which Johnston turned into two catches for 101 yards. The Chargers are averaging only 168.2 passing yards per game this season -- which ranks 28th in the NFL -- and they face a Rams defense that boasts the fourth-best pass defense in the league (186.3 passing yards allowed per game).

items.head: Five snags in defeat
items.body: Gadsden caught all five of his targets for 52 yards during Sunday's 24-9 loss to the Rams. Gadsden was able to lead the team in catches while he finished with one fewer target than team leader Ladd McConkey. The tight end has now reeled in at least three passes for the second straight game and third time over the last four contests after having failed to do so in any of the team's first three regular-season games. Gadsden and the rest of the Chargers will face a tough test in Week 9 against the Texans.

items.head: Active in Week 8
items.body: Gadsden is active for Sunday's Week 8 matchup against the Rams. The second-year tight end has had a relatively quiet first season to date in coordinator Mike McDaniel's offense, posting a 12-103-1 line on 21 targets through six games. Gadsden did get back on the Chargers' offense's radar before the Week 7 bye, recording three receptions for 17 yards on five targets over 33 snaps in Week 6 against the Chiefs after being blanked over 39 plays in Week 5 against the Broncos. It remains to be seen if Los Angeles, which declined to make a change at playcaller during the bye, cooked up some improvements during the idle week, and if Gadsden will be more involved moving forward after flashing plenty of upside as a rookie in 2025 with a 49-664-3 line across 15 reg

items.head: Five grabs in Week 8 win
items.body: Mayer caught five of six targets for 53 yards in Sunday's 38-33 win over the Jets. Mayer's six targets were second on the team behind Brock Bowers' 10, and only Bowers (26) ran more routes than Mayer's 20 on Kirk Cousins' 27 dropbacks. The tight end has just one touchdown this season but has remained an integral part of Las Vegas' passing attack. He's already surpassed his 2025 catches and yards totals, posting 36 grabs for 351 yards through eight games this season. Mayer will be a fantasy TE2 for next Sunday's date with the 49ers.

items.head: Gets 15 touches in Week 8 loss
items.body: Mitchell rushed 11 times for 34 yards and caught four of six targets for three yards in Sunday's 27-10 loss to the Commanders. Mitchell led the team in rushing yards while notching two fewer carries than Saquon Barkley, who was in and out of the game while playing through a back injury. Jaydon Blue, whom the Eagles signed from their practice squad Wednesday, contributed primarily as a special-teams kickoff returner while notching one catch and no carries. Mitchell has been elevated from the practice squad for each of Philadelphia's last two games, so he'll be eligible for one more elevation in Week 9 against the Giants before the Eagles have to sign him to the active roster to keep using him on game days.

items.head: Five catches in win
items.body: Williams caught five of seven targets for 54 yards during Sunday night's 27-10 win over the Eagles. Williams led the team in catches and targets while finishing second behind fellow wide receiver Treylon Burks (81) in receiving yards. With Terry McLaurin (knee) done for the year, Williams will have an opportunity to keep carving out a larger role for himself each week with Washington. On the year, the rookie wide receiver has now reeled in 23 of 33 targets for 259 yards and one touchdown over seven regular-season contests.

items.head: Runs for 36 yards in SNF win
items.body: Ekeler rushed eight times for 36 yards in Sunday night's 27-10 win over the Eagles. The veteran running back wasn't targeted in the passing game on a night when Jayden Daniels attempted 29 passes. Involved in a three-way backfield that also includes Rachaad White and Jeremy McNichols (foot), Ekeler has minimal fantasy appeal headed into next Sunday's matchup with the Rams' strong defense. Jacory Croskey-Merritt (foot) is required to miss at least one more game on injured reserve.

items.head: Four catches in Week 8
items.body: Goedert caught all four of his targets for 30 yards and added a two-yard run in Sunday's 27-10 loss to the Commanders. Goedert has 15 catches for 139 receiving yards in three games since Tanner McKee took over as Philadelphia's starting QB, but the veteran TE has now gone five consecutive appearances without a TD after scoring 13 times in the span of 15 regular-season appearances through Week 1 of this season. Goedert had a ball bounce off his hands for an interception in the second half, but the play was negated by a defensive penalty, removing what would have been the lone blemish on Goedert's otherwise clean, though unimpressive, stat sheet. He'll try to snap his touchdown drought in Week 9 against the Giants.

items.head: Steps up late as team's top RB
items.body: White rushed 11 times for 55 yards and a touchdown while catching two of three targets for five yards in Sunday's 27-10 win over the Eagles. Most of White's production came during a three-play span on Washington's final possession, as he ripped off a 33-yard run down to the four-yard line, followed by a three-yard gain and a one-yard touchdown run to put the game out of reach. The Commanders have divided up backfield duties while Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) is on IR, as Austin Ekeler notched eight carries, while Jeremy McNichols (foot) had five carries and one catch prior to exiting in the second half. White continues to have the highest touch floor among Washington's available running backs heading into Week 9 against the Rams, and he has scored in three of the last four games, with the previous two touchdowns both coming on

items.head: Short TD in loss to Denver
items.body: Gray caught both of his targets for 15 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 28-24 loss to the Broncos. The Chiefs' TE2 caught a four-yard score in the third quarter, his first touchdown of the season. Kansas City uses plenty of 12 personnel, deploying both Travis Kelce and Gray on offense, but Gray handles more of the blocking duties. On the season, he has 14 grabs for 173 yards and a touchdown. There isn't much meat on the bone here for fantasy purposes.

items.head: Scores fifth TD in Week 8 win
items.body: Diggs caught three of six targets for 38 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 19-10 win over the Eagles. Diggs scored an eight-yard touchdown in the second quarter, and the ensuing PAT tied the score at 10-10. That was the team-leading fifth receiving touchdown for Diggs in six appearances with the Commanders. He's the top option for Jayden Daniels on paper since Terry McLaurin sustained a season-ending knee injury in Washington's previous game, though Treylon Burks (81) and Antonio Williams (54) both had more receiving yards Sunday, and Williams also drew one more target than Diggs to lead the team. Diggs is poised to maintain a prominent role in Week 9 against the stout Rams secondary.

items.head: Secures two catches in loss
items.body: Dotson caught two of five targets for 95 yards during Sunday's 16-0 loss to Tampa Bay. Dotson and the rest of the Falcons offense were held in check for the majority of Sunday's loss. The wide receiver did provide Atlanta's biggest highlight play of the day, connecting with quarterback Michael Penix for a 76-yard gain on the team's final possession of the day in the fourth quarter. Dotson's 95 yards were a season high, and he has now reeled in 14 of 31 targets for 337 yards and two touchdowns over eight contests to open the 2026 regular season.

items.head: Modest numbers in Week 8 win
items.body: Daniels completed 16 of 29 passes for 217 yards and a touchdown while rushing twice for 23 yards in Sunday's 27-10 win over the Eagles. Daniels found Stefon Diggs for an eight-yard touchdown in the second quarter and led four drives that ended in successful field goals before Rachaad White sealed the deal with a one-yard touchdown run late in the fourth quarter. Diggs has been on the receiving end of four of Daniels' six touchdown passes this season. Daniels threw for 300 yards in a Week 6 loss to the 49ers prior to Washington's Week 7 bye, but he hasn't exceeded 233 passing yards in any of his 11 other regular-season outings since the start of the 2025 campaign. Sunday night's win over Philadelphia marked Daniels' first win since Week 5 of the 2025 season, when Washington defeated the Chargers. The Commanders will take a 2-

items.head: Records six grabs in loss
items.body: Sampson rushed one time for seven yards and caught six of eight targets for 62 yards in Sunday's 27-6 loss to the Steelers. Sampson was out-carried 11 to one by Quinshon Judkins, but the former has carved out a role as the preferred pass-catching back for Cleveland since returning from injured reserve in Week 7. Over the last two games, Sampson has turned 11 targets into nine catches for 94 yards while adding seven carries for 52 yards. Sampson will have some PPR fantasy appeal during weeks when the Browns are projected to trail on the scoreboard.

items.head: Scores goal-line rushing TD in win
items.body: Freiermuth caught both of his targets for 35 yards in Sunday's 27-6 win over the Browns. He added one rushing attempt for a one-yard touchdown. With time expiring in the second quarter, Freiermuth took a direct snap and punched in a one-yard rushing score to put the Steelers up 20-6 headed into halftime. The tight end entered the season with zero career carries but now has four through eight games, turning them into five yards and a touchdown. As a receiver, Freiermuth has been held to exactly two catches in each of the last three games and has yet to hit 50 yards in any game this season. He's a touchdown-or-bust fantasy bet with the Steelers headed into their bye week.

items.head: Reels in highlight touchdown
items.body: Williams caught his lone target for a 43-yard touchdown during Sunday's 24-19 win over the Dolphins. Williams made the most of his only touch in Week 8, scoring on a 43-yard deep ball from Drake Maye in the third quarter. The wide receiver had an opportunity to be more involved with A.J. Brown (knee) sidelined Sunday, but Williams saw just one target for the third game in a row. On the year, the wide receiver has now caught seven of 13 targets for 190 yards and two touchdowns over eight regular-season contests.

items.head: Catches TD in overtime loss
items.body: Flournoy caught three of four targets for 38 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 33-30 overtime loss to the Cardinals. Flournoy ran 26 routes on Dak Prescott's 38 dropbacks against Arizona, and with Dallas moving more toward three-wide sets and away from multiple tight-end sets while decreasing Jake Ferguson's (ankle) playing time, Flournoy has been a big beneficiary in recent weeks. Over the last four weeks, Flournoy has recorded 238 yards and two touchdowns on 18 grabs across 21 targets. He's achieved WR4 valuation in fantasy and would receive a major boost if CeeDee Lamb or George Pickens ever went down with an injury.

items.head: Pops up for 5-71-1 without Tate
items.body: Dike caught five of six targets for 61 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 43-36 overtime loss to the Bengals. With Carnell Tate (shoulder) inactive against Cincinnati, Dike receiving the biggest playing-time boost on offense, as he ran 40 routes on Cam Ward's 46 dropbacks. Only Gunnar Helm produced more receiving yards than Dike in the Week 8 defeat, and only Wan'Dale Robinson (six) recorded more catches. With the Titans headed into their Week 9 bye, Tate figures to be back the following week versus Jacksonville. Perhaps Dike can earn more playing time at Elic Ayomanor's expense, and Calvin Ridley's name has been linked to trade speculation.

items.head: Snags short TD in loss to Pats
items.body: Washington caught five of six targets for 40 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 24-19 loss to New England. The five grabs led the team on the afternoon, and Washington capped his performance with a one-yard TD from Malik Willis just before halftime. It was Washington's first score of the season in seven games, and he'll take a 31-329-1 line on 45 targets into a Week 9 meeting with the Lions.

items.head: Good to go for Week 8
items.body: Washington (knee) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Patriots, C. Isaiah Smalls II of the Miami Herald reports. Washington practiced fully Friday after limited sessions Wednesday and Thursday. The Dolphins' WR1 in terms of playing time and targets, Washington still hasn't found the end zone this season, producing 26 catches for 289 yards on 39 targets. He's a low-ceiling WR4 in fantasy.

items.head: Finds paydirt in loss
items.body: Coleman caught all three of his targets for 46 yards and a touchdown during Sunday's 24-19 loss to the Patriots. Coleman led the team in receiving yards while reeling in multiple passes for the second time this season. The wide receiver's biggest moment of the game came in the fourth quarter when he connected with quarterback Malik Willis for a 35-yard score with 2:04 remaining in regulation. Coleman hasn't been a consistent part of the team's offensive approach this season, catching eight of 21 targets for 82 yards and two scores over seven contests so far.

items.head: Leading rusher in Week 8 loss
items.body: Gordon carried the ball 19 times for 69 yards in Sunday's 24-19 loss to the Patriots. He failed to catch his only target. For the first time since De'Von Achane (knee) went down in Week 3 and Gordon became Miami's lead back, the second-year player was held out of the end zone. Over the last four games, Gordon has amassed 360 rushing yards and three TDs on 71 totes (5.1 yards per carry), but he's added exactly zero receiving yards to his totals. Gordon will try to begin a new TD streak in Week 9 against the Lions.

items.head: Leads team in receiving in loss
items.body: Allen caught all seven targets for 67 yards in Sunday's 42-7 loss to the Jaguars. The veteran wideout finished second on the team in targets, three behind Tyler Warren on a day Colts QBs attempted 30 passes. When on the field this season, Allen has been a consistent target-earner who runs routes that are friendly to quarterbacks in the short areas of the field. Not a big-play threat whatsoever at this stage of his career, Allen is averaging a career-low 9.0 yards per catch on 36 grabs this season. He has just one touchdown and is a low-upside WR4 for fantasy purposes headed into next Sunday's game against the Cowboys.

items.head: Tosses two TDs in loss to Pats
items.body: Willis completed 21 of 32 passes for 211 yards and two touchdowns with one interception in Sunday's 24-19 loss to New England. He gained two rushing yards on his only carry. The 27-year-old QB hit Malik Washington for a one-yard score just before halftime to give the Dolphins a 13-3 lead, but Willis' 35-yard strike to Kevin Coleman late in the fourth quarter was too little, too late after the Patriots dominated the second half. After throwing just one touchdown over the first four games of the season, Willis has a 5:3 TD:INT in the last three contests while adding two scores on the ground.
